admin.demoteLosesEveryAdminSurface: They lose every /admin page and the cross-tenant reads behind it. Only another app admin, or the CLI, can give it back.
admin.membershipsCouldNotBeRead: The organizations could not be read.

admin.openSessions: {count, plural, =0 {No sessions open} =1 {1 session open} other {# sessions open}}
admin.permanentlyRemovesUserTheir: Permanently removes the user, their conversations, and credit balance. This can't be undone.
admin.promoteGrantsEveryTenant: They gain every /admin page and every permission in every organization on this deployment, including ones they are not a member of.
admin.sessionsCouldNotBeRead: The sessions could not be read.
admin.suspendSignsThemOutImmediately: They are signed out immediately and cannot sign in again until somebody reactivates the account.

agentPin.failed: The agent could not be added to the home screen.

agentTemplates.bringsSkills: {count, plural, =1 {Installs 1 skill with it} other {Installs # skills with it}}
agentTemplates.description: Ready-made agents by industry. Installing one creates a draft you finish and publish.

agentTemplates.title: Agent templates

agents.a2aAuthHint: Callers send an organization API key or an OAuth access token from this deployment as a bearer token, and it must be allowed to run this agent.
agents.a2aDescription: Let other systems' agents send this agent tasks over the A2A protocol. Each task is a run of the published version, under its budget and approvals, and shows in Activity.
agents.a2aOff: Off. Turn it on to give this agent an agent card other systems can find it by.
agents.a2aPublishFirst: Publish the agent first: what A2A serves is the published version.
agents.addAtLeastOne: Add at least one site - a widget allowed nowhere cannot open.
agents.addToAgentHint: Pick the agent. Its draft changes; publish it in the Builder to make it live.
agents.addedFirstMessageEach: Added to the first message of each conversation. It never replaces the agent's own instructions.
agents.alertApprovalsTrigger: A tool call parked, and the run is waiting on a person to decide.
agents.alertBudgetTrigger: A run stopped because this agent reached its own monthly cap.
agents.alertUsageTrigger: Weekly and monthly, what this agent alone has spent.
agents.alertsDescription: Who hears about this agent when nobody is watching it. A run started from chat says what happened on screen; the same run started by a schedule, a channel or the API stops silently, and this is what closes that gap. <link>Your own switches</link> still apply on top and can only ever remove you from a list.
agents.answersCustomerQuestionsFrom: Answers customer questions from the product wiki.
agents.approvalHintDefaultReadOnly: Runs without approval, because this capability only reads.
agents.approvalHintDefaultSideEffecting: Runs without approval, though this capability changes something outside the agent. Choose Always ask if a person should see each call first.
agents.approvalHintNeverReadOnly: No approval, which is what this capability would do anyway.
agents.approvalHintNeverSideEffecting: The agent acts unattended. Only for actions your organization has decided are safe.
agents.approvalHintRequired: A person approves every call before it runs.
agents.approvalParksTheRun: A tool that asks for approval parks the run until somebody answers in this dashboard, so on a chat platform the thread sits there meanwhile - which reads as the bot being broken. For an agent people reach from a channel, the workable setting is a shell that is not gated, inside a container with no network.
agents.archived: Agent archived. Its history and runs are kept.
agents.artifactPagesDetail: Bind the artifact-pages skill and the agent builds pages from its templates, the served chart library and your organization's style - edit the skill to set your brand. The agent reads it through the Skills capability, so switch that on too.
agents.artifactPagesMissing: This organization has no artifact-pages skill. Seed the bundled skills to add it.
agents.audienceAdminsHint: This organization's owners and admins, plus the deployment's app admins.
agents.audienceChosenHint: A standing list, whoever happened to run it.
agents.audienceInitiatorHint: Nobody, for a run a schedule or a channel started.
agents.audienceOwnerHint: The person who would fix this agent's configuration.
agents.backAsDraft: {name} is back as a draft - publish it to run it
agents.backendComputerConsent: Each person chooses a folder or Whole computer the first time they message this agent in the desktop app; the choice is remembered for the agent. This setting grants no access and stores no personal path. A hosted chat must use the desktop app for this workspace.
agents.backendComputerDetail: Use the person’s computer, approved once per agent in the desktop app.
agents.backendServiceDetail: Files and a shell, on a sandbox connection your operator registered.
agents.backendStateDetail: Files but no shell, stored here. Works on every deployment.
agents.behindBy: {count, plural, =1 {1 version behind} other {# versions behind}}
agents.botTokenHintSlack: The bot user OAuth token (xoxb-...) from your Slack app
agents.botTokenHintTelegram: The token @BotFather gives you when you create a bot
agents.botsReady: {count, plural, =1 {1 bot ready} other {# bots ready}}
agents.capabilityHasNoToolSettings: It used to have settings per tool, which it no longer has. Its approval is the one below now.
agents.capabilityToolCount: {count, plural, =0 {Built in, no tools} =1 {1 tool} other {# tools}}
agents.capabilityUsesNoSecret: This capability uses no secret, so the one selected for it would be stored and never read. Publishing refuses it.
agents.channelCanOverrideScope: Each channel this agent is published to can override it.
agents.channelLookupsHint: Channel name, topic and a limited visible member snapshot are added automatically. These switches grant extra actions; file delivery requires a user request.
agents.channelLookupsOn: What this agent may do on {platform}
agents.channelPromptHint: Runtime adds the platform, sender connection state and current channel data on every run. This editable text adds instructions for this binding; new bindings include formatting and channel conversation guidance.
agents.channelPromptPlaceholder: What this agent should know about answering here.
agents.channelRunFreelyHint: Linked channel senders use these settings with the full room history, including messages from other people. Run freely allows calls without another confirmation; use it only for tools and rooms you trust.
agents.claudeTokenHint: On a Claude Pro or Max subscription: run claude setup-token on your own computer and add the token it prints as a key here. An Anthropic API key works too.
agents.codeModeHint: The agent calls its tools from one short Python script in a sandbox - loops, conditions, many calls at once - instead of one model turn per call. Worth it for working through records or fanning out over an MCP server. Tools that need approval stay ordinary calls.
agents.codingAgentKeyName: {signIn, select, chatgpt {OpenAI key for Codex} other {Claude Code key}}
agents.collectionScopeHint: The model chooses what to look for; it can never widen where it looks. <link>Manage collections</link>
agents.collectionsDetail: What this agent may search. A collection it is not given is one it cannot reach, however the question is phrased.
agents.collectionsOffButBound: Knowledge search is switched off, so none of these collections are searched. They stay in the spec and are still checked at publish; switch it on above, or unpick them.
agents.connectionNoLongerAllows: This connection no longer allows {runtime}. Pick one it does, or the agent fails on its first tool call.
agents.considerOnlyMostLikely: Consider only the most likely tokens making up this much probability mass. Set this or temperature, not both.
agents.contextCount: {count, plural, =1 {1 context file} other {# context files}}
agents.contextFilesDetail: Standing context this agent reads - a glossary or policy injected into its prompt, or files it reads on demand.
agents.contextInjectOnlyNoTools: Every file bound here is injected into the prompt, so the read tools (list_context, read_context) are not attached - the agent already has the text and has nothing to read on demand. Set a file to linked to give it the tools.
agents.contextLoadingHint: An injected file is added to every run; a linked one the agent reads only when it decides it is relevant. <link>Manage context</link>
agents.contextOffButBound: Context is switched off, so none of these files reach the model - not the injected ones either, because the injection happens here. They stay in the spec and are still checked at publish; switch it on above, or unpick them.
agents.costReportingHint: Whether a reply says what the turn cost. It is recorded either way - 'the bot went quiet' is a question somebody asks days later.
agents.councilMembersProviderHint: Choose a different provider for each council member.
agents.createdDraft: Created {name} - a draft, nothing published yet

defaultBadge.classifierHint: Reads the answers for every knowledge base's gaps.
defaultBadge.drafterHint: Drafts what every knowledge base is missing.
defaultBadge.generatorHint: Drafts the cases every dataset asks for.
defaultBadge.improverHint: Proposes the improvements every agent is offered.
defaultBadge.judgeHint: Grades every dataset that has no judge of its own.

agents.delegateNameClash: Something else here is also called {name}. The model addresses a subagent by name, so one of the two would never be reached.
agents.delegatePinBehind: {by, plural, =1 {One version behind} other {# versions behind}}: pinned at v{version}, and v{latest} is what this delegate publishes now. Nothing changes here until you say so.
agents.delegatePinGoneDetail: This version no longer exists, so a run that reaches this delegate fails and names it. There is deliberately no fall back to the current version.
agents.delegatePinnedTwice: Pinned twice. Two pins of one agent are two delegates answering to one name, so the model cannot say which it meant - and the spec refuses it before it reaches the server.
agents.delegateUnreachableDetail: This organization no longer has it, or you may not see it. Publishing will refuse it either way - remove it, or ask for access to it.
agents.delegatesDetail: Published agents this one may hand work to, each frozen at a version.
agents.delegatingNeedsRunPermission: Delegating needs permission to run agents, which you do not have here. Publishing checks each delegate against the publisher's own access, so this is the same refusal, earlier.
agents.delegationModeAsyncDetail: The parent keeps working and collects the answer later. Worth it for one slow specialist, and a poor default.
agents.delegationModeAutoDetail: The parent's model chooses per call. It has the task in front of it, and nothing else does.
agents.delegationModeFollowDetail: Whatever the policy below says, so changing it moves every delegate that never disagreed.
agents.delegationModeSyncDetail: The parent stops until the delegate answers. The default, and what makes a delegation read like a function call.
agents.delegationOffButConfigured: Delegation is switched off, so none of this is reached. The delegates below stay in the spec and are still checked at publish - switch it on above, or remove them.
agents.delegationPolicyDetail: What bounds every delegation this agent makes, delegates and specialists alike.
agents.delegationPolicyNoSchema: This deployment's delegation capability publishes no configuration schema, so there is nothing to set here. Depth, fan-out and mode arrive with it.
agents.deploymentSOwnShortlist: This deployment's own shortlist - the provider could not be asked. Any id it accepts still works.
agents.diffTooLong: Too long to compare line by line.
agents.draftDiffersHint: The draft is saved. Everything published - channels, widgets, the API - keeps answering with v{version} until you publish.
agents.eachPersonsOwnAccountShort: Everyone connects their own; not for API keys, the widget or routines.
agents.embedDictationBrowserHint: The visitor's browser transcribes and sends the audio to its vendor - Google, Apple and others. Nothing reaches this deployment, and not every browser offers it.
agents.embedDictationServerDrift: No speech-to-text provider answers for this agent right now, so visitors see no microphone until one does.
agents.embedDictationServerHint: Recorded in the page and transcribed by this organization's speech-to-text provider, on the organization's bill. The audio isn't stored.
agents.embedDictationServerUnavailable: Server needs a speech-to-text provider with a credential, chosen on the organization's Voice card or on this agent's.
agents.embedDictationServerUnchecked: Server can't be checked right now: this agent's speech-to-text readiness didn't load. Reload the page to try again.
agents.embedVoiceDrift: Visitors see no call button until this agent can take calls again.
agents.embedVoiceHint: Visitors can call the agent. They can't approve anything, so tools that need approval are left out of their calls. Calls count against the budgets.
agents.embedVoiceUnavailable: Voice calls need a voice set up on this agent's Voice card.
agents.embedVoiceUnchecked: Voice calls can't be checked right now: this agent's call readiness didn't load. Reload the page to try again.
agents.everyPageCarryingIts: Every page carrying its key stops working immediately. The key cannot be reissued - a new widget gets a new one.
agents.everyRunAlreadyTraced: Every run is already traced into the Logfire project this deployment is configured with. Pick a write token to send this agent's runs to a project of its own instead - an agent built for a client traces into the client's project, with their retention and their alerting.
agents.everyToolFollowsThis: Every tool follows this until you answer for it separately.
agents.everyoneWhoTalksAgent: Everyone who talks to this agent reads and writes the same files. A file one person uploads is visible to the rest of the organization. Publishing this is recorded in the audit log.
agents.failedReleaseMode: The release mode could not be saved
agents.failedTestConnections: The test connections could not be saved
agents.filesWorkspaceHasNo: The Files workspace has no shell - pair it with Run Python to compute.
agents.gatewayLitellmProxyModel: A gateway, a LiteLLM proxy, or a model server on this network. Give one and the key becomes optional - there is nothing to authenticate against on your own hardware.
agents.guardsStarted: {count, plural, =0 {Nothing to run - every guard has passed or is already checking} =1 {Started 1 eval suite} other {Started # eval suites}}
agents.handleDescription: It will be mentioned as <at>{handle}</at>, which is fixed once created and is how Slack and the API address it.
agents.hostOperatorRegisteredCredential: A host an operator registered. The credential lives in the vault, not in this spec.
agents.hostedIntegration: Link - for somebody with no site of their own
agents.hostedLinkProtection: Anyone with the link can talk to this agent. What protects it is that the key cannot be guessed, plus this embed's rate limit, its budget and its pause switch - nothing else.
agents.hostedLogoHint: Whichever you upload elsewhere - there is no second upload here, and no URL for this page to go fetching.
agents.hostedLogoLimits: PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF, up to 2MB.
agents.hostedLogoPublishFirst: Publish the page first - an upload needs somewhere to go. The picture can be added the moment it exists.
agents.hostedRequiredNotUrlSafe: Required and not URL-safe: {names}. A hosted page can only be told a variable through its own URL, so mark it URL-safe or make it optional.
agents.hostedTitleHint: Shown in the browser tab. Empty uses the agent's name.
agents.hostedWelcomeHint: Shown above the composer before the first question. The agent never sees it, so it is not a turn it thinks it took.
agents.howAgentsReferModel: How agents refer to this model
agents.howLongOneModel: How long one model request may take before it is abandoned.
agents.howVariedAnswerNear: How varied the answer is. Near 0 for classification and extraction, higher for drafting. Some providers cap this at 1, and reasoning models reject it entirely - leave it alone there.
agents.imageModelDetail: Every model this provider can be asked to draw with.
agents.imageModelUnknownProvider: This binding names {provider}, which cannot draw. Pick a provider above.
agents.imageProviderDetail: Only providers whose models can be given the image tool are offered; the platform asks the SDK rather than keeping a list.
agents.imageProvidersUnavailable: The list of providers could not be read. The model above is still what will be used.
agents.inDraftOf: {more, plural, =0 {In the draft of {names}, not published yet} other {In the drafts of {names} and # more, not published yet}}
agents.judgeAgreement: People agreed with this judge on {agreed} of {decided, plural, =1 {1 result} other {# results}} they decided.
agents.judgeAgreementNone: Nobody has decided a result this judge graded yet, so there is no agreement to show.
agents.judgeDatasetNothing: This judge has graded nothing in this dataset yet.
agents.judgeDatasetOpen: Show what this judge graded in {name}
agents.judgeDatasetSeeAll: See all on the Review tab
agents.judgeDatasetsHint: The datasets that picked this judge, grading or not. A dataset picks its judge on its Grading tab; open one to see what the judge graded there.
agents.judgeUnused: No dataset uses this judge yet.
agents.leaveEmptyProviderS: Leave empty for the provider's own API
agents.listedByProviderJust: Listed by the provider just now.
agents.longestAnswerModelMay: The longest answer the model may generate.
agents.manageOwnAccounts: Rename or choose your main account in MCP servers
agents.mapArchivedDetail: This delegate has been archived since it was pinned, so every run that reaches it is refused. Unarchive it, or repin this agent without it.
agents.mapCycleDetail: Delegation returns to an agent already above it on this branch. A run refuses the loop rather than following it.
agents.mapDepthCapDetail: Has delegates of its own that a run starting from this agent can never reach - the delegation depth cap stops here, or its delegation is switched off.
agents.mapPinBehindDetail: This delegate has published past the pinned version. Nothing changes here until somebody repins it.
agents.mapSpecialistDetail: Defined inside this agent, with no page of its own.
agents.mapTreeLoading: Walking the delegation tree - delegates below the first level are not drawn yet.
agents.mapTreeTruncated: The delegation tree is larger than one response walks, so its deepest parts are not drawn.
agents.mapTreeUnavailable: The full delegation tree could not be loaded, so only direct delegates are shown.
agents.mattermostServerUrlHint: The address you open Mattermost at in the browser, without a path
agents.mattermostWebhookTokenHint: The token Mattermost shows for the outgoing webhook
agents.mentionableOnBoundBots: Slack, Microsoft Teams, Telegram, Mattermost and Discord bots that answer as this agent. It is mentionable by @handle only on the bots it is bound to.
agents.menuArchiveHint: Out of the pickers; its history stays
agents.menuAvatarHint: The picture people recognise it by
agents.menuDeleteHint: Gone for good, with every version
agents.menuDuplicateHint: A draft copy to change freely
agents.menuExportHint: The spec as YAML, to keep in a repository
agents.menuRestoreHint: Back in the pickers, as it was
agents.modelApiFromModelHint: Stav.ai serves most models on Chat Completions and a few only on Responses. The model decides.
agents.modelApiFromModelPending: Chosen from the model when it is saved
agents.modelApiHint: OpenAI's own API serves every model on Responses, and its newest models on nothing else. Most OpenAI-compatible servers (vLLM, LM Studio) implement only Chat Completions.
agents.modelApiHintAzure: Responses needs a recent api_version on the Azure key; Chat Completions works with any.
agents.modelHasNoKeyHint: This model's key was deleted from the vault, so nothing can run on it. Give it a key in the model panel, or choose another model.
agents.modelIdOpenRouterHint: Namespaced by origin, as OpenRouter lists it - openai/gpt-5, anthropic/claude-opus-5.
agents.modelIdOtariHint: Use provider:model or an alias/routing policy defined in your Otari gateway.
agents.modelIdProviderHint: As the provider names it. Free text, because they ship new ones faster than any list here could be updated.
agents.modelRegionHint: Where Stav.ai may run this model's requests. It answers only from endpoints in the region and refuses a request it cannot serve there.
agents.modelsCouldNotBeListedHint: This panel is empty because the request for this organization's models did not answer, not because it has none.
agents.name: Name
agents.namedSoOrganizationCan: Named, so an organization can rotate a key or repoint every agent at once.
agents.nativeClientOriginNote: A browser sends an Origin header for you. A client of your own must set one that is on the allowed-sites list below, or the socket closes with 4003.
agents.newStarterPlaceholder: What can you help me with?
agents.noAgentToAddTo: There is no agent to add it to yet.
agents.noBotAskAdmin: No bot yet - an admin adds one
agents.noDelegatesYet: No delegates yet. Only a published agent can be one - there is a version to pin.
agents.noKeyForEndpoint: No key - the endpoint needs none
agents.noMembersChooseFrom: No members to choose from - this organization is just you.
agents.noModelAskAdmin: Models are added in the Builder by a member who manages connections. Once one exists, it can be chosen here.
agents.noProviderKeyAddOneHere: No {provider} key in the vault yet. Add one here and it is stored for every agent in this organization.
agents.noProviderKeyAskSomebody: No {provider} key in the vault yet, and storing one needs a permission you do not hold. Somebody who can manage this organization's vault has to add it before this model will run.
agents.noRemoteAgentsRegistered: No remote agents are registered yet. <link>Register one</link> by its agent card.
agents.noSecretSelected: Nothing chosen yet - the agent cannot be published until something is.
agents.noSitesAllowedWidget: No sites allowed - this widget cannot open anywhere
agents.noSpecialistsYet: No specialists. One is worth adding when publishing a whole agent would be too much ceremony for the job.
agents.nobodySetHearAdd: Nobody is set to hear this. Add an audience, or switch the alert off.
agents.notAChatModelHint: {model} is not a chat model - it is for text to speech, transcription, images or embeddings, and an agent cannot run on it. Choose a chat model before publishing.
agents.notAChatModelRefused: {model} is not a chat model - an agent cannot run on it. Choose a chat model.
agents.notIndexedCount: {count, plural, =1 {1 not indexed} other {# not indexed}}
agents.notPublishedAnySite: Not published to any site yet.
agents.nothingToShareWithDelegates: This agent is bound to nothing else, so there is nothing to pass on.
agents.offRemovesShellEntirely: Off removes the shell entirely, rather than asking before each command.
agents.onePerLineDifferent: One per line. A different port or subdomain is a different site - the browser treats them as such, so this list has to.
agents.openRouterEndpointHint: Leave empty for the global OpenRouter API, or enter a regional URL such as https://eu.openrouter.ai/api/v1. EU routing requires an eligible OpenRouter plan; ZDR is configured separately on OpenRouter.
agents.optionalPointModelAt: Optional. Point this model at a gateway or proxy instead of the provider's own API; the key is still what authenticates.
agents.organizationAposSOwn: The organization's own monthly cap is not here. It stops every agent in the organization and an agent's author cannot raise it, so its alert always goes to the admins.
agents.organizationHasNoCollections: This organization has no collections yet. An agent with none searches nothing.
agents.organizationHasNoContext: This organization has no context files yet.
agents.organizationHasNoModels: This organization has no models yet. An agent cannot run without one.
agents.organizationHasNone: The organization has no {name} account yet.
agents.organizationHasRegisteredNo: This organization has registered no sandbox connection, so this agent cannot be published with a container. An operator adds one under Sandboxes.
agents.organizationHasWrittenNo: This organization has written no skills yet.
agents.originsSocketHint: A browser sends Origin for you; a client of your own sends nothing unless you set it, and an unset one is refused with close code 4003.
agents.orphanedCollections: This agent also references {count, plural, =1 {1 collection} other {# collections}} this organization no longer has. Publishing is refused until they are cleared:
agents.orphanedContext: This agent also references {count, plural, =1 {1 context file} other {# context files}} this organization no longer has. Publishing is refused until they are cleared:
agents.orphanedServers: This agent also references {count, plural, =1 {1 server} other {# servers}} this organization does not offer - removed since, or carried in from an imported spec. Publishing is refused until they are cleared:
agents.orphanedSkills: This agent also references {count, plural, =1 {1 skill} other {# skills}} this organization no longer has. Publishing is refused until they are cleared:
agents.otariEndpointHint: Enter the gateway URL ending in /api/v1 before loading models. Hosted: https://api.otari.ai/api/v1. EU: https://eu.api.otari.ai/api/v1.
agents.pageAllowFiles: A way to attach a file
agents.pageAllowFilesHint: The only thing here that lets a stranger store something on this deployment. The file goes through the same checks and parser a member's upload does, under a smaller cap and a limit per visitor - and the agent reads it the way it reads any attachment.
agents.pageAllowNewConversation: A button to start a fresh thread
agents.pageAllowNewConversationHint: The old thread is not deleted. It stops being the one this browser resumes.
agents.pageShowThinkingHint: What the model says to itself before it answers. It is not written for anybody to read and it is not an answer you can stand behind.
agents.pageShowToolResultsHint: The arguments a step was called with and what came back. Written for the model, so this is where something internal turns up - an address, a row from a system, a passage nobody meant to publish.
agents.pageShowToolStepsHint: One line per step - Searching the documents, Running a query. On, because a page that goes quiet for thirty seconds reads as broken.
agents.pageShows: What the visitor sees of the work
agents.pageShowsHint: These decide what the server sends, not what the page draws. A visitor who opens devtools sees exactly what is ticked here and nothing else.
agents.pausedHandleAnswersNothing: Paused - the handle answers nothing here.
agents.personalConnectedState: {count, plural, =1 {You are connected.} other {You have # accounts connected, and it reaches all of them.}} Everyone else connects theirs the first time they chat.
agents.personalNotConnectedState: Everyone connects their own. You have not connected yours yet.
agents.platformActsAsWhoeverAsks: Every tool acts as the person the agent runs for, with exactly their permissions. Nothing new is granted: what they could not do in the console, the agent cannot do here either.
agents.platformAllHint: Every call waits for approval, reading included.
agents.platformServerDescription: This platform's own tools: agents, runs, spend, knowledge bases, skills and members - so the agent can answer questions about the platform and act in it.
agents.platformWritesHint: Reading is free; creating, running or changing anything waits for the person to approve it.
agents.productionHint: Channels, widgets and the API answer with v{version}: production runs it until a newer version is promoted.
agents.promoteSpecialistDetail: Creates a draft agent from this specialist. It is not published, not pinned as a delegate, and this specialist stays where it is.
agents.providerPublishesNoList: This provider publishes no list here. Type the model id as the provider names it.
agents.publicSurfacesDescription: A published agent already answers in this dashboard and through the API. These are the surfaces you open to the public - each one runs the same frozen version, under the same budget and the same approval gate.
agents.publishFirstCreatesProduction: This is the first publish, so it creates production on v{version} - the agent has to have somewhere to run.
agents.publishFreezesDraft: The draft is frozen as v{version} - a published version never changes.
agents.publishGuardedChecks: {count, plural, one {# guard suite} other {# guard suites}}
agents.publishGuardedFollower: {name} is guarded by {guards}: it moves to v{version} only after all guards pass.
agents.publishMovesFollower: {name} follows every publish, so it moves to v{version}.
agents.publishPinnedStays: {name} stays on v{version} until you promote.
agents.remoteDelegateGone: A remote agent no longer registered
agents.remoteDelegateGoneDetail: Its registration was removed, so publishing refuses this agent until it is taken off the list.
agents.remoteDelegatesDetail: Other vendors' agents this one may hand work to over A2A. Each call goes under this agent's budget.
agents.reviewerInstructionsPlaceholder: Flag claims that have no source among the pages the agent read.
agents.reviewersDescription: A second, usually cheaper model reads the run every few requests and sends one short correction when it drifts. Its calls count against the budget like any other, and a run without a reviewer makes no extra calls.
agents.runningThemOneAt: Running them one at a time makes a conversation easier to follow, and easier to approve.
agents.runtimesUnreadable: {error} Until it answers, the runtimes it allows cannot be listed here.
agents.scopeAgentDetail: One shared workspace for the whole organization.
agents.scopeChannelDetail: Every thread in one channel shares. Direct messages stay separate.
agents.scopeConversationDetail: Everyone in the chat. On Slack a thread is a chat, so threads do not share.
agents.scopeUserDetail: One workspace per person, across every surface they reach this agent on.
agents.scriptTagIntegration: Script tag - for a site you do not control
agents.secretForDifferentService: Key "{name}" is for a different service. Choose a key for this configuration.
agents.secretMissingFromVault: The secret selected here is not in this organization's vault - it was deleted, or the spec was written against another organization. Publishing refuses it.
agents.secretOfWrongKind: "{name}" is of kind {kind}; this capability needs {needed}. Publishing refuses it.
agents.secretUnchanged: Leave blank to keep the stored secret
agents.separateEndpointHint: Save this endpoint as a separate model to keep the current profile for other agents. “Update model” changes the shared profile wherever it is used.
agents.separatesStagingTrafficFrom: Separates staging traffic from the real thing in the same project.
agents.serverInThisAgent: Whose account, which tools, and which wait for you.
agents.shareWithDelegatesDetail: A delegate runs on its own spec. Only what this agent is itself bound to can be shared, so a delegate is never the quiet route to a capability nobody granted.
agents.skillLoadingHint: The agent loads a skill only when it decides one is relevant, so twenty skills cost almost nothing in context. <link>Manage skills</link>
agents.skillsDetail: Written know-how the agent loads only when it decides a skill is relevant, so twenty skills cost almost nothing in context.
agents.skillsOffButBound: Skills is switched off, so none of these are loaded - the agent is resolved with them and then reads none. They stay in the spec and are still checked at publish; switch it on above, or unpick them.
agents.socketIntegration: WebSocket - for an interface you are building
agents.specialistDescriptionDetail: What the parent's model reads when deciding whether to delegate here - the highest-leverage sentence in a delegation. “Researches a topic and cites sources” gets used; “helper” does not.
agents.specialistNameBlank: A specialist the model cannot address is one it cannot use.
agents.specialistNameClash: Something else here is also called {name}, so one of the two would never be reached.
agents.specialistNamePattern: Letters, digits, underscores and dashes only. The model emits this verbatim.
agents.specialistNameTooLong: At most 64 characters - it becomes a tool argument.
agents.specialistsNotVersioned: Defined here, not published: a specialist has no version, cannot be pinned, and changes the moment this agent is edited.
agents.speechAccountVoiceDetail: {provider} voices belong to your account. Paste the id of one from your voice library. It is the default - the agent may switch to another per clip, among the voices allowed below.
agents.speechAnyAccountVoiceWarning: None listed: the agent may speak in any voice in your {provider} account by its id - cloned voices included.
agents.speechAnyVoiceWarning: {count, plural, =1 {None allowed: the agent may speak in this model's one voice.} other {None allowed: the agent may speak in any of this model's # voices.}}
agents.speechFormatDetail: The formats this provider returns. mp3 is smaller, wav is uncompressed.
agents.speechModelDetail: Every model this provider can be asked to speak with.
agents.speechModelUnknownProvider: This binding names {provider}, which cannot speak. Pick a provider above.
agents.speechOtherVoiceNotePlaceholder: Who it is, e.g. Anna, the narrator
agents.speechOtherVoicesDetail: The only voices the agent may switch to, clip by clip - for a dialogue, or a narrator and a character.
agents.speechOtherVoicesFull: {count} other voices is the most one agent can be offered.
agents.speechProviderDetail: The providers in the speech catalog whose key the vault can hold.
agents.speechProvidersUnavailable: The list of providers could not be read. The model above is still what will be used.
agents.speechVoiceDetail: The default - the agent may switch to another per clip, among the voices allowed below.
agents.staleCollections: {count, plural, =1 {1 knowledge collection} other {# knowledge collections}}
agents.staleContext: {count, plural, =1 {1 context file} other {# context files}}
agents.staleReferences: This draft still references {list} this organization no longer has. Publishing is refused until they are cleared.
agents.staleServers: {count, plural, =1 {1 MCP server} other {# MCP servers}}
agents.starterMessageLabel: Message shown below the title and sent on click
agents.startersHint: What the chat offers somebody opening this agent for the first time - one click sends one. Up to {max}; with none, the chat shows its own.
agents.startsAsDraftNothing: It starts as a draft. Nothing runs until you publish it.
agents.startsWithRecommended: {count, plural, =0 {Starts with no tools} =1 {Starts with 1 recommended tool} other {Starts with # recommended tools}}
agents.stavEndpointHint: Leave empty for api.stav.ai. Set it only for a regional or test endpoint of Stav.ai.
agents.storeInVaultHint: <link>Store one in the vault</link> and it appears here - this shape has several fields, so it is filled in there. The value stays in the vault; an agent records which secret to use, never the secret.
agents.storedVaultNeverShown: Stored in the vault and never shown again. Your backend signs each visitor a HS256 token with it.
agents.storedVaultUnderTracing: Stored in the vault under Tracing. The spec keeps the reference, never the token.
agents.surfaceApiBody: Run the agent from your own backend with an organization API key. Nothing to publish here.
agents.surfaceApiNotes: The API needs a credential your organization already has, and no per-agent setup, so there is nothing on this screen to configure. Whoever holds the key runs the agent as the caller it belongs to.
agents.surfaceDashboardAlways: Any member who can see this agent can already chat with it in the dashboard. That needs nothing here.
agents.surfacePageBody: A link we serve, at /e/ plus the key. No site of your own and nothing to paste - what protects it is the key being unguessable, plus the rate limit and the budget.
agents.surfaceSocketBody: The protocol the widget speaks, for an interface you build yourself: a mobile app, a kiosk, a component in your own design system.
agents.surfaceWidgetBody: A chat bubble on a site you do not control. One script tag, no build step. The list of allowed sites is what protects it, because the key in the tag is public.
agents.systemAgentBadge: {kind, select, judge {System agent · Judge} drafter {System agent · Gap drafter} generator {System agent · Case generator} classifier {System agent · Gap classifier} improver {System agent · Authoring assistant} other {System agent}}
agents.systemAgentBadgeHint: The platform runs it for the whole organization; nobody chats with it.
agents.systemAgentKnowledgeHelp: {kind, select, judge {Checks facts in an answer against the knowledge bases of the agent it grades, where no reference answer states them.} generator {Searches the knowledge bases you draft cases from, so questions follow what they really say.} classifier {Checks whether the knowledge base already answers a question before calling it a gap.} drafter {Searches the gap's knowledge base, so a draft does not repeat what a document already says.} improver {Reads the knowledge bases of the agent it improves, so its changes fit what they hold.} other {Searches the knowledge bases the platform picks for each run.}}
agents.systemAgentMaxStepsHint: Each step is a paid request on every answer it reads. At most {max}; left empty, {fallback}.
agents.systemAgentRouteBody: The platform runs it for the whole organization and nobody chats with it, so it is never tested in an eval or improved here. Change how it works on its own page.
agents.systemAgentSharedOnly: Only what is shared with the whole organization is offered: the platform runs this agent for everyone.
agents.systemAgentSkillsUnused: A classifier reads no skills, so none can be added here. Unpick the ones it still holds, or use its switch to take them all off.

systemChoice.hint: The published model and instructions are configured on the helper’s agent page.
systemChoice.label: Run with
systemChoice.loadFailed: Could not load available agents. Try again.
systemChoice.only: Runs with {helper}, the organization's default. <link>Change it on its page</link>.

agents.temperatureVariesVerdict: {kind, select, judge {Above 0, the same answer can be graded differently twice. 0 keeps grades repeatable.} other {Above 0, the same answer can be labelled differently twice. 0 keeps labels repeatable.}}
agents.testConnectionsHint: Runs in this environment, evals included, answer each binding below with its test system. A binding switched off here does nothing - it never falls back to production.
agents.testPanelChangesWhy: The draft under test against version {version}, the one published.
agents.testPanelCompareHint: Ask both chats from the box below so they receive the same prompt.
agents.testPanelDraftSaving: Saving your latest change - send once it is saved to test it.
agents.testPanelPinPlaceholder: Ask, or pin a prompt to rerun…
agents.testPinnedHint: Pinned - ask it again after each change
agents.testSideUnusable: Off here: the test connection is disabled or not signed in
agents.testStarterIdentityPrompt: Who are you, and who built you?
agents.testStarterOffTopicPrompt: Can you write me a short poem about the weather?
agents.testStarterScopePrompt: What can you help me with?
agents.testWelcomeDraft: Answers as your unpublished draft, as a test run. Nothing is published, and it is billed like any run.
agents.testWelcomeVersion: Answers as the published version this environment serves, as a test run.
agents.toolNameBlank: The model calls the tool by this name, so it cannot be blank.
agents.toolNamePattern: Letters, digits and underscores only - the model calls this name verbatim.
agents.toolNameSteersModel: A tool's name and description are the prompt the model reads before it decides to call it, so both steer it: <mono>{reached}</mono> is reached for on questions <mono>{passed}</mono> is passed over for. Edits here apply to this agent alone.
agents.toolsAfterConnecting: Its tools are listed once a {name} account is connected.
agents.traceContentFull: Full - messages, output and tool calls
agents.traceContentHint: "None" keeps timing, tokens, cost and tool names but sends no message text or tool arguments - for a project over health, legal or HR data.
agents.unavailableDescription: Check the selected organization. This agent may belong to another organization, have been removed, or no longer be shared with you.
agents.unchangedLines: {count, plural, =1 {1 unchanged line} other {# unchanged lines}}
agents.updateModelHint: Saves the new key, endpoint or API on {label}. Everything that uses this model switches with it: every agent, and any collection or scheduled work on it. To leave those as they are, choose “Name it something else” and add a separate model.
agents.urlSafeHint: A hosted page can only be told a variable through its own URL, and a URL is something the visitor types. Mark only what is safe for them to set.
agents.usedBy: {more, plural, =0 {Used by {names}} other {Used by {names} and # more}}
agents.usedByNobody: Not used by any agent yet
agents.variableDescriptionPlaceholder: Which plan this visitor is on
agents.variableNameRule: Lower-case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter.
agents.variableNameTaken: That name is already a variable.
agents.variablesHint: Write '{{name}}' in the instructions, or click one to insert it. They are filled in when each conversation starts.
agents.vaultCouldNotBeRead: The vault could not be read
agents.vaultUnreadableDetail: The vault could not be read, so nothing can be chosen here - which says nothing about what your organization has stored. Listing secrets needs the permission that manages connections. {error}
agents.videoAspectRatioDetail: The default - the agent may ask for another shape this model renders, per clip.
agents.videoAudioDetail: The default - the agent may ask for sound on or off, per clip.
agents.videoLengthDecided: This model decides its own length, {min} to {max} seconds.
agents.videoLengthRange: This model makes clips of {min} to {max} seconds.
agents.videoMaxResolutionAnyWarning: With no highest resolution, the agent may ask for any resolution this model renders, up to {highest}, and a second at a higher resolution costs more.
agents.videoMaxResolutionDetail: The one limit on the resolution: the agent may ask for anything up to it.
agents.videoModelDetail: Every model this provider can be asked to make video with.
agents.videoModelUnknownProvider: This binding names {provider}, which cannot make video. Pick a provider above.
agents.videoProviderDetail: The providers in the video catalog whose key the vault can hold.
agents.videoProvidersUnavailable: The list of providers could not be read. The model above is still what will be used.
agents.videoResolutionDetail: The default - the agent may ask for another per clip, up to the highest resolution below. Higher costs more per second.
agents.visualDesignDetail: Bind the visual-design skill and the agent draws from its house style and templates - architecture diagrams, explainers with sliders, 3D scenes. Switching Visuals on binds it for you; the agent reads it through the Skills capability.
agents.visualDesignMissing: This organization has no visual-design skill. Seed the bundled skills to add it.
agents.voiceCallsLead: A live, two-way conversation: the agent listens, answers out loud and keeps its tools. People call it from the chat, the website widget and the hosted page. Runs on a realtime voice model.
agents.voiceConversationCatalogFailed: The list of voice models could not be loaded, so calls cannot be turned on here. Reload the page to try again.
agents.voiceConversationDeploymentHint: The Azure OpenAI deployment calls go to. The endpoint comes from the key.
agents.voiceConversationEnabledHint: Off until you switch it on. Takes effect when the agent is published.
agents.voiceConversationGuardrails: Guardrails check transcripts during a call and cut the agent off when its words hit one, but spoken words cannot be filtered before they are heard. A tool's result is still screened before the agent reads it; tool arguments are not screened.
agents.voiceConversationLanguageHint: The language the agent speaks in calls.
agents.voiceConversationMaxHint: Calls end at this length. The budgets still apply.
agents.voiceConversationNoteHint: Added to the agent's instructions only during calls, after its built-in speaking style: how to greet, how long to talk, what to say before a tool runs.
agents.voiceConversationNotePlaceholder: Greet the caller by name. Keep each answer to two sentences, then ask whether they want more detail.
agents.voiceConversationVoiceHint: How the agent sounds in calls.
agents.voiceDescription: How people can talk to this agent: a live voice call, or dictation that turns speech into text. Takes effect when the agent is published.
agents.voiceDictationLead: Speech turned into text that the person reads before sending: the microphone in the chat, and voice notes sent to this agent's channel bots. Runs on a transcription model.
agents.voiceDictationProviderHint: The chat microphone sends the recording to the provider below: the organization's, or this agent's own. Off, or with no key to send it with, the browser transcribes it for free.
agents.voiceInheritsUntilChosen: Until you choose one, the organization's is used: {pair}
agents.voiceLanguageHint: A fixed language is more accurate than auto-detect.
agents.voiceNoteChannelsOnly: The browser transcribes chat dictation to this agent, so the provider below only changes how voice notes sent to its channel bots are transcribed.
agents.voiceNoteNoProvider: Neither the organization nor this agent has a speech-to-text provider, so the browser keeps transcribing until you choose one here.
agents.voiceOrgNoPair: The organization has no provider set, so there is nothing to inherit.
agents.voicePreviewNeedsKey: Choose a key to listen to this voice
agents.voiceProviderHint: From the speech-to-text catalog. Sent with the key chosen below.
agents.whatAgentCalledLogfire: What the agent is called in Logfire.
agents.whatServiceAllowsNever: What the service allows. It never names an image - that is the operator's decision.
agents.whatThePageSuppliesHint: Set these on the page as window.AgenticOSContext before the widget script loads. They are appended to the agent's instructions as information about the visitor - never as instructions, because a value from a browser is one a visitor can edit.
agents.widgetGreetingHint: Drawn by the widget before anybody types. It is never sent to the model - a greeting in the model's history is a turn the agent thinks it took.
agents.widgetPublished: Widget published. Copy the snippet into your site.
agents.widgetQuickRepliesHint: Up to four, offered under the greeting. A click sends one as the visitor.
agents.widgetRemoved: Widget removed. Every page carrying its key has stopped working.
agents.widgetShowSources: Name the sources an answer used
agents.widgetShowSourcesHint: Lists the documents from your knowledge base under an answer - their names only, never the passages.
agents.workflowTablesViaMcp: Workflows and Tables are tools in the AgenticOS MCP server. Add it under MCP servers and select the tools this agent needs. Existing capability bindings keep their saved grants.
agents.workflowsGrantsDetail: Each becomes something the agent can run - with the input it declares, as the member the agent acts for, and waiting for its answer.
agents.workflowsNone: No workflow yet. Build one and publish it to start by hand, by the API or by a call.
agents.workflowsOrphaned: A workflow this agent was given is gone:
agents.workflowsStartsElsewhere: Starts on its own trigger. An agent starts only workflows begun by hand, by the API or by a call.
agents.youArePricingPage: You are on the pricing page. Answer in German.
agents.youNotVisitorsWhich: For you, not for visitors - which placement this is.
agents.yourBackendSignsToken: Your backend signs a token we verify

answerFormat.agentsOwnHint: The agent's own answer format: text, or the object its answer format names.
answerFormat.description: Whether the agent answers in prose or with data of a fixed shape - for an API, a workflow step or a system that reads the answer.
answerFormat.fieldDescriptionPlaceholder: What goes here, in a line the model reads

invalid.notObject: The schema must describe an object: "type": "object".

answerFormat.label: It answers
answerFormat.structuredHint: An object with these fields. The model is asked for it and sent back to fix an answer that does not fit; the API returns it as structured, the chat shows it as JSON.
answerFormat.textHint: Free-form prose, as in a chat.
answerFormat.title: Answer format

apiKeys.accessWhy: What the key may do. It holds only permissions you have, and narrows again if your role changes.
apiKeys.couldNotLoad: Could not load your API keys
apiKeys.createWhy: Name it after what will use it, so you know which one to revoke.
apiKeys.createdWhy: This is the only time it is shown. Only a fingerprint of it is stored.
apiKeys.emptyWhy: Create one to call the API from a script, Postman or Claude Code.
apiKeys.name: Name
apiKeys.personalConsentWhy: Personal consent is excluded from presets. To let this key or app approve routines and watches that use your personal connections and data, select personal:consent under Custom.
apiKeys.revokeWhy: Anything using this key stops working immediately. This cannot be undone.
apiKeys.searchHint: Try a key name, prefix or the email of its issuer.
apiKeys.shownOnce: Copy it now and keep it somewhere safe. If you lose it, revoke it and create another.
apiKeys.title: API keys
apiKeys.useItLikeThis: Send it as a bearer token:
apiKeys.why: Keys let a script, an HTTP client or an MCP client call this organization's API as you, narrowed to what you pick. A key never does more than you can today.

apiReference.authBody: Send the key in the Authorization: Bearer aos_… header. It acts in the organization it was issued in, with the permissions it was issued with and never more than its issuer holds now, and it is rate limited on its own.
apiReference.description: Every endpoint an API key can call on this deployment (version {version}), read from its own OpenAPI document. Open an endpoint for its parameters, body, responses and a ready curl call.
apiReference.loadError: The API reference could not be loaded.
apiReference.name: Name
apiReference.title: API reference

apiUsage.auth: Send the key in the Authorization: Bearer aos_… header.
apiUsage.title: Use the API
apiUsage.why: Everything an API key can do, over plain HTTP: run agents, read runs and what they cost, fill and search knowledge bases, manage members. Create a key below, then call the base URL.

appConnections.callbackPending: Authorization is not ready yet. Check the account below or reconnect.
appConnections.catalogHint: Browse the Composio app catalog or search for an app. Recommendations are based on your goal; every app asks for its own authorization.
appConnections.catalogUnavailable: The full app catalog is temporarily unavailable. Your existing accounts and configured apps remain accessible.
appConnections.checkFailed: The latest check could not verify access. Reconnect or try checking again.
appConnections.connectFailed: We could not start authorization. Please try again.
appConnections.consentHint: Continue to authorize this app, then return here to verify the connection.
appConnections.defaultHint: The default account is used when no account is specified. Other connected accounts remain available.
appConnections.description: Bring the tools you already use into T3OS. Start with one useful task.
appConnections.disconnectHint: Remove {account} from T3OS. Agents and routines that rely on this connection will need another account or a new connection.
appConnections.exploreApp: Explore this app with my assistant
appConnections.exploreAppPrompt: Help me get started with my connected {toolkit} account {account} (connection {connection}; service {catalog}). Describe a few useful tasks using the available tools and ask which I want to try. Do not call app tools until I choose a task. Use only this account.
appConnections.firstTaskHint: Choose an account and ask your assistant to complete a real task. The result opens in your assistant conversation.
appConnections.firstTaskNeedsAccount: Connect and verify an app for this task first. You can also skip setup and explore T3OS.
appConnections.goalHint: Choose a starting point. You can connect more apps later.

answers.description: Turn project notes into clear next steps.
answers.prompt: Use only my connected {toolkit} account {account} (connection {connection}; service {catalog}) to find a small set of recent project notes and summarize priorities, decisions, and open questions. Read only; do not change anything. Do not switch accounts. Cite the sources you used and ask me to narrow the project if the available context is ambiguous.
answers.title: Find project answers

day.description: A useful brief before your first meeting.
day.prompt: Use only my connected {toolkit} account {account} (connection {connection}; service {catalog}) to summarize today's upcoming meetings and what I should prepare. Read only; do not create, change, or send anything. Do not switch to a different account. Include source links where available, and explain any missing access rather than inventing a result.
day.title: Prepare my day

inbox.description: Find the messages that need your attention.
inbox.prompt: Use only my connected {toolkit} account {account} (connection {connection}; service {catalog}) to summarize a small set of recent messages that need my attention and suggest next steps. Read only; do not send, delete, archive, or change anything. Do not switch accounts. Include source links where available, and explain any missing access rather than inventing a result.
inbox.title: Review my inbox

artifacts.addSiteTitle: Add a site to the public link?
artifacts.addSiteWhy: A new site means more people can see this page's data, so the public link hides it until it's confirmed again.
artifacts.archiveWhy: Nobody can open it and the agent can't publish it again, and its public link turns off. Everything is kept, so you can restore it later.
artifacts.archivedWhy: Nobody can open this page and the agent can't publish it again. After a restore, its public link stays off until you turn it on.
artifacts.askForAccess: Ask an administrator for access to apps.
artifacts.cannotSee: You cannot see this organization's apps

changeOwner.confirm: {name} becomes the owner of this page. Its data is hidden from others until {name} confirms it, and automatic sharing turns off. {name} and the previous owner are notified.
changeOwner.confirmSelf: {name} becomes the owner of this page. Its data is hidden from others until {name} confirms it, and automatic sharing turns off. {name} is notified.
changeOwner.title: Change owner of {title}
changeOwner.why: Hand the page to another member. They become its owner at once.

consent.awaitingForYou: The data appears once the page's owner confirms it.

artifacts.couldNotLoad: This app could not be loaded
artifacts.deleteWhy: Every version and the public link go with it, and nobody it was shared with can open it any more. The agent makes a new one the next time it publishes under this name.
artifacts.description: Apps your agents published - reports, small dashboards, summaries. Each one keeps its link when the agent publishes it again, and its earlier versions stay readable.
artifacts.embedNeedsNoPassword: An app behind a password cannot be embedded. Remove the password to embed it.
artifacts.embedSiteCount: {count, plural, one {# embedding site} other {# embedding sites}}
artifacts.embedSitesWhy: One site per line. Only these can put the app in an iframe.
artifacts.followed: You will be notified when a new version is published
