max_steps.description: How many steps one call may take; each step is one model request. A task that needs more continues in the same tab on the next call.

vision.title: Show the model screenshots
vision.description: Send each step's screenshot to the model as well as the page's elements. Better on visual pages, more tokens, and the model has to read images.

candidate_cap.title: Elements offered per step
candidate_cap.description: How many of the page's elements may be offered as choices in one step. Lower is cheaper and blinder; the answer to a page too dense for the cap is to scroll.

preview.title: Show a live preview
preview.description: Send the viewport to the chat while the browse runs, so a person can watch it. Costs one JPEG per step on the socket.

preview_width.title: Viewport width (pixels)
preview_width.description: The browser's viewport width in pixels, which is also how wide the frames are. It decides what the agent can see without scrolling.

step_model_profile_id.title: Model for each browse step
step_model_profile_id.description: A model profile `browse_web` asks for each step instead of the agent's own. Steps are most of a browse's time and cost, so a cheaper model here makes a long browse cheaper, and quicker where its provider answers quickly - measure it, since a small model through a slow gateway is no faster. Empty uses the agent's model. The agent's own browser tools always use it.

connection.title: How the browser reaches the web
connection.description: Built in uses the deployment's browser and its address. A proxy sends the browses through an address of your own - a residential or regional one sites block less. A hosted browser runs them in a browser service you pay for, reached over CDP. This computer requires a paired desktop and local browsing selected for this chat.

proxy_url.title: Proxy address
proxy_url.description: http://, https:// or socks5:// with the host and port. Its username:password goes in the vault, picked below; Chromium cannot sign in to a SOCKS proxy.

hosted_url.title: Hosted browser address
hosted_url.description: The service's wss:// CDP address. Its key goes in the vault, picked below, and is added to the address's query when the browse connects.

hosted_key_param.title: Query parameter for the key
hosted_key_param.description: What the hosted browser calls its key in the address's query.

timezone.title: Time zone the browser reports
timezone.description: An IANA time zone such as Europe/Warsaw. Set it to match the proxy's region: a browser whose clock and address disagree reads as a bot.

locale.title: Language the browser reports
locale.description: A language tag such as pl-PL, sent as Accept-Language and navigator.language.

prefer_native_browser.title: Use the native local browser
prefer_native_browser.description: Use an embedded native tab for local DOM browsing. Disable for isolated Chromium compatibility. Vision and language/time-zone overrides use Chromium.

tools.title: Allowed lookups
tools.description: Which channel lookups this binding allows, by tool id. Empty means none, which is what a binding starts as.

default_limit.title: Results when no number is asked for
default_limit.description: Members, search results or messages returned when the model does not ask for a number

timezone.title: Time zone
timezone.description: IANA timezone the agent thinks in, e.g. Europe/Warsaw

timeout_secs.title: Time limit per call (seconds)
timeout_secs.description: Wall-clock budget for one call, in seconds

max_memory_mb.title: Memory limit per call (MB)
max_memory_mb.description: Memory cap for one call, in megabytes

strategy.title: Strategy
strategy.description: Which strategy to apply when the history approaches the window

max_fraction.title: Start at this share of the window
max_fraction.description: Fraction of the model's context window at which compaction starts

keep_messages.title: Recent messages kept
keep_messages.description: How many recent messages survive a summary or a sliding window

keep_tool_pairs.title: Recent tool results kept
keep_tool_pairs.description: How many recent tool calls keep their results when results are cleared

summary_prompt.title: Summary prompt
summary_prompt.description: What the summarising model is told. `{messages}` is where the conversation being replaced is inserted, and it is required - a prompt without it summarises nothing. Edit it to keep what your agent's work depends on: the default keeps intent, decisions and open threads, which is not the same as what a support transcript or a code review needs

context_window.title: Context window override
context_window.description: Override the window this triggers against. Also what the chat's context gauge divides by, so the two describe one ceiling. Set it when the resolved number is wrong for your deployment - a beta or a tier can be given less than the provider publishes - or to make an agent compact earlier than its model would require

fallback_context_window.title: Fallback context window
fallback_context_window.description: Window to assume when the model's own cannot be resolved

expose_read_tool.title: Let the agent open linked files
expose_read_tool.description: Whether link-mode files are reachable through a read tool. Off means only injected files reach the model, and nothing is read on demand.

file_settings.title: How each file is used
file_settings.description: Per-agent mode and availability for attached context files. An absent entry preserves the file's legacy defaults.

max_results.title: Conversations per search
max_results.description: How many conversations one search returns at most. Each brings back a short passage, so a high number costs context on every search.

members.title: Council members
members.description: The delegates, one strong model from each of three different providers at high reasoning effort. Exactly three members.

agreement_threshold.title: Agreement threshold
agreement_threshold.description: The score out of 10 every delegate must reach for a round to satisfy the council. A round below it means fix and review again.

max_rounds.title: Rounds at most
max_rounds.description: How many review rounds one run may ask for. A fresh review after fixes is a new round, and the cap is what stops repeated reviews turning into scope creep.

redact_secrets_in.title: Hide secrets in the question
redact_secrets_in.description: Redact API keys and tokens from the user's prompt

redact_pii_in.title: Hide personal data in the question
redact_pii_in.description: Redact emails, phone numbers, IBANs, cards and SSNs from the prompt

blocked_keywords_in.title: Blocked words in the question
blocked_keywords_in.description: Block the run if the prompt contains any of these terms (comma or newline separated)

redact_secrets_out.title: Hide secrets in the answer
redact_secrets_out.description: Redact API keys and tokens from the agent's answer

redact_pii_out.title: Hide personal data in the answer
redact_pii_out.description: Redact emails, phone numbers, IBANs, cards and SSNs from the answer

blocked_keywords_out.title: Blocked words in the answer
blocked_keywords_out.description: Block the run if the answer contains any of these terms (comma or newline separated)

redact_secrets_tool.title: Hide secrets in tool results
redact_secrets_tool.description: Redact API keys and tokens from tool results before the model reads them

redact_pii_tool.title: Hide personal data in tool results
redact_pii_tool.description: Redact emails, phone numbers, IBANs, cards and SSNs from tool results

blocked_keywords_tool.title: Blocked words in tool results
blocked_keywords_tool.description: Block the run if a tool result contains any of these terms (comma or newline separated)

redact_secrets_args.title: Hide secrets in tool arguments
redact_secrets_args.description: Redact API keys and tokens from the arguments the agent passes a tool

redact_pii_args.title: Hide personal data in tool arguments
redact_pii_args.description: Redact emails, phone numbers, IBANs, cards and SSNs from tool arguments

blocked_keywords_args.title: Blocked words in tool arguments
blocked_keywords_args.description: Block the run if a tool's arguments contain any of these terms (comma or newline separated)

phone_regions.title: Phone number countries
phone_regions.description: Countries whose national phone formats PII redaction reads, as two-letter codes (comma or newline separated), at most 16 regions and 256 characters. A number written with + is redacted whatever is listed

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: Whose model draws. Only providers whose model class honours the image tool are accepted - three today - and which those are is asked of the SDK rather than listed here.

model.title: Image model
model.description: Which of that provider's image models draws, by the ids in `app/core/catalog/image_models.json`. A model outside the catalog is refused: the tool answers a model that cannot draw with an error its author only sees mid-run.

quality.title: Quality
quality.description: Rendering quality; higher is slower and dearer.

size.title: Size
size.description: Output size. OpenAI uses the pixel values, Google the K values.

background.title: Background
background.description: Background type; transparent needs a png or webp output.

default_top_k.title: Passages per search
default_top_k.description: Passages returned when the model does not ask for a number

self_query_enabled.title: Infer filters from the question
self_query_enabled.description: Infer FA-039 business filters (source, document type, organizational unit, date range) from the natural-language query with an LLM when the model searches without naming any filter itself. Off by default. Each such search makes one extra model request, billed to the run. It can only narrow within the agent's tenant and collections, never widen.

query_analysis_mode.title: Query expansion
query_analysis_mode.description: Optionally analyse and expand the query before retrieval to improve recall on short or fuzzy questions. Off by default. `multi_query` and `hyde` each make one extra model call

query_analysis_max_variants.title: Rephrasings at most
query_analysis_max_variants.description: How many rephrasings `multi_query` may add, bounding its fan-out and cost. Ignored by the other modes

parent_context.title: Include the surrounding text
parent_context.description: Small-to-big retrieval: return each matched chunk with the text around it. Matching and ranking always run on the small chunks, the matched chunk is never shortened, and the added context is bounded.

threshold_bytes.title: Store parts larger than (bytes)
threshold_bytes.description: Binary or text parts at least this large are written to storage and replaced with a reference in the stored history.

allow_personal.title: Keep private notes per person
allow_personal.description: Whether the agent keeps private notes for each person it talks to, readable only when it is alone with them. Off drops that store entirely, for compliance or privacy; the notes it keeps in group chats stay.

enable_subtasks.title: Subtasks and dependencies
enable_subtasks.description: Adds subtasks and dependencies: a step waits as blocked until the steps before it finish. Off by default, because a flat checklist is enough for most work.

cache_ttl.title: Legacy prompt cache lifetime
cache_ttl.description: Kept so existing agent specs still load. Planning no longer uses this value; configure prompt caching through cache in the model settings.

backend.title: Where files live
backend.description: state: files only, no shell, stored by the platform - works on every deployment with no extra services. service: a container or cloud sandbox, on one of the connections this organization has registered. local: the person selects and approves their own computer in desktop chat; no machine path or native consent is stored in this spec.

connection_id.title: Sandbox connection
connection_id.description: Which registered sandbox connection to run on; empty takes the organization's default. An id, never an address or a token - a spec is exported to a client's git repository, so the only thing it may carry is a reference. The connection decides whether that is a container on a host you run or a sandbox in Daytona's cloud.

session_scope.title: Who shares the workspace
session_scope.description: Who shares one workspace: run (a fresh one every turn), conversation (everyone in the chat or Slack thread), channel (a whole Slack channel), user (one person across chats) or agent (everyone who talks to it).

runtime.title: Runtime
runtime.description: Which environment a container-backed workspace runs, named from the list the connection's service allows. Empty takes the connection's default. An alias, never an image.

include_execute.title: Allow shell commands
include_execute.description: Whether the agent may run shell commands. Turning it off leaves the file tools and removes the shell entirely, rather than gating it.

max_tuning_runs.title: Tuning runs at most
max_tuning_runs.description: How many tuning runs one run may record. A fresh tuning run after a proposal is applied is a new run, and the cap is what stops repeated scoring turning into scope creep.

reviewer.title: Reviewer
reviewer.description: The one reviewer that judges the work, on its Sol model.

max_rounds.title: Rounds at most
max_rounds.description: How many review rounds one run may ask for. A fresh review after fixes is a new round, and the cap is what stops repeated reviews turning into scope creep. Extend to 5 only for security, permissions, auth, data loss, or state and concurrency, while a blocker or should stays open - or when the user asks.

inline.title: Inline specialists
inline.description: Specialists defined inside this agent, for work that does not justify publishing an agent of its own. Not versioned: editing this agent changes them, and nothing else can reference them.

mode.title: Delegation mode
mode.description: Sync waits for the delegate's answer, async collects it later, auto lets the model choose per task. A background delegation cannot wait for an approval, so keep work that needs one on sync.

allow_questions.title: Let delegates ask questions
allow_questions.description: Lets a delegate ask the person waiting a question instead of guessing. Works only for a sync delegation, and only for the specialists this agent was given. A question is not an approval and cannot grant one.

allow_dynamic.title: Let the agent create specialists
allow_dynamic.description: Lets this agent write its own specialists while it runs. Each is instructions and one of your models, with no tools or knowledge, spends from this run's budget and is gone after the reply. Gate `create_agent` to see each one first.

max_depth.title: Delegation depth
max_depth.description: How many levels of delegation are allowed, counting this agent. 1 lets it delegate but not its delegates; 2 allows one nested level. Each level multiplies the requests one turn can make.

max_fanout.title: Delegations at once
max_fanout.description: How many delegations may run at once. Reached, the next one is refused with a message the model can act on rather than an error. This is the ceiling on a background delegation launching a background delegation until a dozen agents are running against one budget.

max_result_chars.title: Answer length shown per delegate
max_result_chars.description: How much of a finished delegation's answer is shown when several are collected at once. A truncated one says so and points at the tool that returns it in full, so nothing is lost - this only decides how much of five specialists' work arrives in one turn's context.

share_with_delegates.title: Capabilities delegates inherit
share_with_delegates.description: Capabilities this agent passes on to its delegates, such as a shared workspace so one writes a file and another reads it. Nothing is shared unless named here, and delegation itself never is.

allow_any_agent.title: Use other accessible agents
allow_any_agent.description: Offer the current published versions of other agents this person may run in this organization, under agent-prefixed slug handles. Explicit pins keep their selected versions. The catalog is resolved at the start of each interactive run; unattended work stays limited to reviewed pins. Large catalogs increase setup time and context.

reminders.title: Fixed reminders
reminders.description: Fixed lines re-stated on their own cadences

goal_reanchor.title: Restate the original request
goal_reanchor.description: Re-state the original request on a cadence, at no token cost

llm_reminder.title: Model-written reminder
llm_reminder.description: A model-written reminder on a cadence. Costs one extra call each fire

cache_ttl.title: Prompt cache lifetime
cache_ttl.description: Cache lifetime of the breakpoint placed before the tail reminder

effort.title: Reasoning effort
effort.description: How hard the model reasons before answering. Leave unset for the provider's own default effort; a level a provider does not have maps to its closest one.

action.title: When a result is too long
action.description: What to do with a return once it is over the threshold

threshold.title: Size limit
threshold.description: Size at or above which a return is reduced. Characters by default; estimated tokens when 'over tokens' is set, where it defaults to 15,000

over_tokens.title: Measure in tokens
over_tokens.description: Measure the threshold in estimated tokens rather than characters

max_chars.title: Characters kept
max_chars.description: Characters kept when a return is truncated, or when a spill or summary falls back to truncation. Left unset, never more than the threshold

truncation_strategy.title: Which part to keep
truncation_strategy.description: Which end(s) of an oversized text to keep when truncating

strip_ansi.title: Strip terminal colours
strip_ansi.description: Strip terminal colour codes from text returns before measuring and reducing

summary_prompt.title: Summary prompt
summary_prompt.description: What the summarising model is told, for the 'summarize' action. Must contain {output}, where the tool's full output is inserted; {tool_name} is available too, for the name of the tool that produced it

strategy.title: Search method
strategy.description: auto: native tool search on a provider that supports it, local keyword matching elsewhere. keywords: always match locally, on any provider. local_bm25: rank identifiers, descriptions and arguments locally on any provider. bm25 / regex: force an Anthropic-native algorithm; errors on a provider that has no native tool search.

max_results.title: Matches per search
max_results.description: How many matches the local search returns; ignored for native search.

defer_capabilities.title: Defer capability tools
defer_capabilities.description: Hide eligible tools from enabled capabilities until the agent searches for them. Off keeps capability tools visible.

defer_mcp_servers.title: Defer MCP tools
defer_mcp_servers.description: Hide eligible tools from bound MCP servers until the agent searches for them. Off keeps MCP tools visible.

exclude_capabilities.title: Always-visible capabilities
exclude_capabilities.description: Comma-separated capability IDs whose tools stay visible, such as knowledge or visuals. These capabilities must still be enabled.

exclude_mcp_servers.title: Always-visible MCP servers
exclude_mcp_servers.description: Comma-separated MCP tool namespace prefixes whose tools stay visible, such as github_work or agenticos. Use the prefix before the tool name, with hyphens replaced by underscores.

exclude_tools.title: Always-visible tools
exclude_tools.description: Comma-separated model-facing tool names to keep visible. Use renamed capability tool names and fully prefixed MCP tool names, such as github_work_list_issues.

method.title: How pages are fetched
method.description: local: we fetch the page, identically on every model. native: the model provider fetches it with its own egress and citations (only on models that support it). auto: native where the model has it, ours everywhere else.

max_content_chars.title: Page length limit (characters)
max_content_chars.description: How much of a page one fetch returns before it is truncated; roughly four characters per token. Ignored under native fetch, which the provider bounds itself.

allowed_domains.title: Allowed domains
allowed_domains.description: Bare hostnames the agent may fetch, e.g. docs.example.com; empty means any. Matched exactly - no wildcards, no subdomains.

blocked_domains.title: Blocked domains
blocked_domains.description: Bare hostnames the agent may never fetch, matched exactly.

method.title: Search engine
method.description: duckduckgo: free, no account, results rendered as clickable sources. native: the model provider searches with its own index and citations (only on models that support it). tavily: summarised for a model to read. brave: an index of its own. exa: search by meaning rather than keywords. keenable: no account needed; an API key is optional.

max_results.title: Results per search
max_results.description: How many results one search returns; ignored for native search.

harness.title: Coding agent
harness.description: Which coding agent does the work: Claude Code, on an Anthropic key or a Claude subscription token, or Codex, on an OpenAI key or a ChatGPT sign-in.

access.title: What it may do
access.description: Change files and run commands, such as tests - or only read the code and answer. Set Human approval to ask before each task either way.

model.title: Model
model.description: The model the coding agent runs: a Claude model for Claude Code, an OpenAI one for Codex. Not set takes the coding agent's own default. Not available on this computer, where the agent uses its own setting.

base_url.title: Anthropic-compatible endpoint
base_url.description: Claude Code only: a gateway that speaks Anthropic's API, such as https://openrouter.ai/api, with the key in the vault being that gateway's. Empty calls Anthropic directly.

timeout_minutes.title: Time limit (minutes)
timeout_minutes.description: How long one task may run before it is stopped.

runs_on.title: Where it runs
runs_on.description: The agent's sandbox with its configured key, a disposable private cloud task using the initiating person's profile account, or the folder a person chooses on their own computer in the desktop app, where Claude Code and Codex use the sign-in they already have and need no key.

harness.title: Harness
harness.description: The CLI session that does the agent's work: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Gemini CLI or Pi.

access.title: Access
access.description: What the harness may do in the agent's sandbox: only read code, or change code and run commands.

model.title: Model
model.description: The model the harness runs on: a Claude model for Claude Code, an OpenAI one for Codex, a Gemini one for Gemini CLI, or any of those vendors' models for OpenCode or Pi. Not set takes the harness's own default.

base_url.title: Anthropic-compatible endpoint
base_url.description: Claude Code only: a gateway that speaks Anthropic's API, such as https://openrouter.ai/api, with the key in the vault being that gateway's. Empty calls Anthropic directly.

timeout_minutes.title: Prompt timeout (minutes)
timeout_minutes.description: How long one prompt may run before it is stopped. The session stays open.

workflow_ids.title: Workflows it may start
workflow_ids.description: Published workflows that start by hand, by the API or by a call.

wait_seconds.title: Wait for a run (seconds)
wait_seconds.description: How long run_workflow waits for a run to finish before handing back its id to read later.

preview_screenshot.title: Show the model a page's picture
preview_screenshot.description: Hand the model the picture of a page when it previews one. Turn off for a model that cannot read images; the written report still comes back.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: Whose voices speak. Offered: the providers in `app/core/catalog/text_to_speech_models.json` whose key the vault can hold.

model.title: Speech model
model.description: Which of that provider's speech models speaks. A model outside the catalog is refused here rather than mid-run.

voice.title: Voice
voice.description: The voice that speaks unless the agent chooses another; left empty, the model's first. ElevenLabs voices belong to your account, so for ElevenLabs paste the voice id from your voice library.

voices.title: Allowed voices
voices.description: The only voices the agent may switch to instead of the one above, per clip - for a dialogue, or a narrator and a character. Left empty, it may choose any voice the model offers - for ElevenLabs, any voice id in your account.

output_format.title: File format
output_format.description: mp3 is smaller, wav is uncompressed. Left empty, the provider's first format - Gemini returns wav only.

max_characters.title: Longest text
max_characters.description: The most text one call may speak, which caps what a single call can cost.

provider.title: Provider
provider.description: Whose model makes the video. Offered: the providers in `app/core/catalog/video_models.json` whose key the vault can hold.

model.title: Video model
model.description: Which of that provider's video models makes the clip. A model outside the catalog is refused here rather than mid-run.

resolution.title: Resolution
resolution.description: The resolution a clip is made at unless the agent asks for another; left empty, the model's first. Higher costs more per second.

max_resolution.title: Highest resolution
max_resolution.description: The highest resolution the agent may ask for, at least the usual one; it caps what a second can cost. Left empty, the agent may ask for any resolution the model renders.

aspect_ratio.title: Aspect ratio
aspect_ratio.description: The shape a clip takes unless the agent asks for another; left empty, the model's first.

seconds.title: Length
seconds.description: Seconds a clip runs unless the agent asks for another length; left empty, five, or the nearest the model makes. Not for a model that decides its own length.

max_seconds.title: Longest clip
max_seconds.description: The longest clip the agent may ask for, which caps what one call can cost; left empty, the model's own limit. Not for a model that decides its own length.

audio.title: Sound
audio.description: Whether clips carry sound unless the agent asks otherwise, where the model makes it optional; left empty, the provider's default.

alibaba_workspace.title: Alibaba workspace
alibaba_workspace.description: Alibaba only: the Model Studio workspace id, which Wan 3.0 is called through. Left empty, the shared DashScope endpoint, which Alibaba keeps for existing integrations.

alibaba_region.title: Alibaba region
alibaba_region.description: Alibaba only: the region the workspace is in.

timeout_seconds.title: Time limit
timeout_seconds.description: How long to wait for a clip, in seconds. A job not finished by then is cancelled where the provider allows it and booked at its estimate.

model_profile_id.title: Model for next steps
model_profile_id.description: A separate model profile that writes next-step buttons in the background after the answer is saved. It never delays the answer or the next message. A small, cheap model is enough. Empty disables next-step suggestions.

desktop.title: Environment
desktop.description: Choose where this agent operates a desktop. The selected environment's requirements are shown below.

daemon_url.title: Daemon URL
daemon_url.description: The computerd endpoint of your desktop. Its host must be on COMPUTER_DAEMON_ALLOWED_HOSTS.

screen_width.title: Screenshot width
screen_width.description: The widest screenshot the model is shown; larger screens are scaled down to fit.

screen_height.title: Screenshot height
screen_height.description: The tallest screenshot the model is shown.

max_actions_per_call.title: Actions per call
max_actions_per_call.description: How many actions one call may send.

max_actions.title: Actions per run
max_actions.description: How many actions one run may take in total.

preview.title: Live preview
preview.description: Show the desktop live in the chat while the agent works it.

endpoint_id.title: Telephone endpoint
endpoint_id.description: The configured Twilio telephone endpoint from Channels. Only explicit member consent and current limits authorize a call.

mounts.title: Folders
mounts.description: What the terminal mounts, each as a folder.

allowed_commands.title: Allowed commands
allowed_commands.description: Only these commands run, e.g. ls, cat, grep. Empty allows virtual commands; direct curl/wget are disabled.

hidden_paths.title: Hidden paths
hidden_paths.description: Paths the agent cannot see at all, e.g. /drive/HR/.

max_message_chars.title: Longest message
max_message_chars.description: The longest message this agent may send, in characters. 16,000 is the console's ceiling as well, so a thread reads the same however the message was sent; lower it for an agent that should keep its messages short.

allow_attachments.title: Allow file attachments
allow_attachments.description: Whether this agent may send files it already uploaded along with its messages. Off means text only; files already attached stay readable.

poll_interval_seconds.title: Poll interval
poll_interval_seconds.description: Seconds between checks of the pull request. At least 60, so the watcher never polls in a tight loop and never burns the shared GitHub rate limit.

max_watch_minutes.title: Watch at most
max_watch_minutes.description: Minutes one watch may run before it stops and reports blocked. A watch that runs past this without green has not been approved — it has expired.

max_subtasks.title: Subtasks at most
max_subtasks.description: How many subtasks one burst runs at once. 3 is the subagents max_fanout default and 10 its hard max: a burst shares that ceiling rather than raising it. Reached, the tool refuses the extra parts with a message the model can act on.

max_bursts.title: Bursts at most
max_bursts.description: How many bursts one run may ask for. A fresh burst after fixes is a new burst, and the cap is what stops repeated bursts turning into scope creep.

agent_messages.does: Lets one agent write directly to another, in a thread the console shows with replies, reactions and files.
agent_messages.example1: Ask the research agent to hand its findings to the writing agent before the draft is due.
agent_messages.name: Agent messages
agent_messages.needs: Two published agents the caller may run, and the agents:run permission to read the thread.
agent_messages.never: Does not reach an agent the caller may not run, send on a human's behalf, or deliver a message outside the thread.

artifacts.does: Lets the agent publish a finished app - a report, a small dashboard - under a link people open in a browser.
artifacts.example2: A one-page project brief to share with a client
artifacts.name: Apps
artifacts.never: Never shares an app by itself: it stays private to the person until they share it.

ask_user.does: Lets the agent ask a few multiple-choice questions instead of guessing.
ask_user.example2: Which of these three files should I use?
ask_user.name: Ask the user
ask_user.never: Never answers for the person. In Slack or Telegram it waits for their reply.

babysit_pr.does: Watches a pull request through CI and review bots, reporting only what changed, and stops when the bots are green on the latest commit.
babysit_pr.example1: Is this pull request green yet?
babysit_pr.example2: Watch this PR and tell me when the checks pass
babysit_pr.name: Babysit PR
babysit_pr.needs: A way to read the PR's checks, such as the monitor capability running `gh pr checks`.
babysit_pr.never: Never merges, comments, or takes any other action on the PR: watching and reporting only.

background_tasks.does: Starts independent work in a fresh topic while you keep talking; returns its result to the original agent.
background_tasks.example1: Investigate the export bug in a new topic while we continue planning the release.
background_tasks.name: Background topics
background_tasks.needs: A published console agent, an active member, and an approved folder for local work.
background_tasks.never: Does not copy the full conversation, waive approvals, restart interrupted actions, or start watches and routines.

background_tools.does: Lets the agent start a slow tool - a long browse - and carry on with the rest of the request, using the result when it arrives.
background_tools.example1: Check three suppliers' portals and draft the email while the browses run
background_tools.name: Work while tools run
background_tools.needs: A capability with a slow tool, such as the web browser.
background_tools.never: Never runs anything after the run ends; stopping the run stops its background tools.

browser_use.does: Gives the agent a real web browser it works step by step - reading pages, clicking, filling forms and searching - to finish a task.
browser_use.example1: Check a supplier's portal for new invoices
browser_use.example2: Fill in a long web form
browser_use.name: Web browser
browser_use.needs: A browser host set up by an administrator. A long task takes a few minutes and one model request per step.
browser_use.never: Never goes outside its allowed domains, and never follows instructions written on a page.

burst.does: Splits one task into independent subtasks, runs them in parallel, and merges the results into one outcome.
burst.example1: Research three approaches at once and merge what they find
burst.example2: Draft the sections of a guide in parallel
burst.name: Burst
burst.needs: A task that splits into independent parts, each with its own prompt.
burst.never: Never drops a failed part or presents the merge as complete while one is failed: a part that fails is reported with its reason.

channel_tools.does: In Slack, Telegram or Mattermost, lets the agent see who is in the channel, what it is for and what was said earlier.
channel_tools.example1: Catch up on a thread before answering
channel_tools.example2: Mention the right person in a reply
channel_tools.name: Chat channel lookup
channel_tools.needs: A bot in that channel. It is switched on per bot, under where the agent is available.
channel_tools.never: Never reads a channel its bot has not been added to.

charts.does: Draws a chart in the conversation, so people see the numbers instead of reading them.
charts.example1: Sales this month by region, as bars
charts.example2: Support tickets per week, as a line
charts.name: Charts
charts.never: Never changes the data it draws.

clock.does: Tells the agent today's date and time, so it does not guess.
clock.example2: How many days until the deadline?
clock.name: Date and time
clock.never: Adds no tools; it only tells the agent the time.

code_execution.does: Lets the agent work out numbers with a short Python program instead of estimating them.
code_execution.example1: Total a column of figures somebody pasted
code_execution.example2: Compare two loan offers month by month
code_execution.name: Calculations
code_execution.never: Keeps nothing between messages and cannot reach the internet. For files that stay, use the Sandbox.

coding_agent.does: Hands software work to Claude Code or Codex, in the agent's sandbox or on this computer, while you watch each step in the chat.
coding_agent.example1: Fix a failing test in a repository the agent cloned
coding_agent.example2: Explain how a module works, read-only
coding_agent.name: Coding agent
coding_agent.needs: For a sandbox: the Sandbox capability, a connection and a provider key or sign-in in the vault. On this computer: the desktop app, a signed-in coding agent and an approved full-access folder.
coding_agent.never: Local tasks require a full-access folder grant and native start confirmation. Set Human approval to Always ask to also approve each task in the chat.

compaction.does: Shortens the oldest part of a long conversation so the agent keeps going instead of hitting the model's limit.
compaction.example1: A working session that lasts all day in one chat
compaction.name: Long conversations
compaction.never: Never deletes the conversation: people still see all of it.

computer_use.does: Lets the agent operate a whole desktop - any application, not only web pages - by looking at screenshots and using the mouse and keyboard. You watch it live in the chat.
computer_use.example1: Fill in a form in a desktop application
computer_use.example2: Export a report from a legacy tool with no API
computer_use.name: Computer use
computer_use.needs: A desktop in the agent's own sandbox (the Sandbox capability on its 'desktop' runtime), or one an administrator runs with computerd on a Linux desktop or a Mac, with its token in the organization's vault. Each step is one model request with a screenshot.
computer_use.never: Never acts without approval unless that is switched off, never follows instructions shown on the screen, and stops to ask before passwords or payments.

context.does: Gives the agent your company's standing information - a glossary, a policy, a brand voice - every time it answers.
context.example1: Always use the product names from the glossary
context.example2: Follow the refund policy word for word
context.name: Context
context.needs: Context files, written under Context and picked in this panel.
context.never: Never changes the files; the agent only reads them.

conversation_search.does: Lets the agent look up what was said in earlier conversations with the same person.
conversation_search.example1: What did we decide about the launch date last week?
conversation_search.example2: Pick up a task where the last chat left off
conversation_search.name: Past conversations
conversation_search.never: Never reads anybody else's conversations, and is off in group chats.

council.does: Asks three delegate reviewers, one strong model from each of three different providers, to score the work out of 10 in parallel rounds until all agree.
council.example1: Is this pull request ready to merge?
council.example2: Score this draft proposal before it goes out
council.name: Council
council.needs: One model profile per delegate, from three different providers.
council.never: Never substitutes a missing delegate or invents a score: a delegate that cannot be reached is reported unavailable, and one that gives no score reads no score.

drafts.does: Shows text the agent writes for you to send - an e-mail, a chat reply, a post - as a card with a copy button on each part.
drafts.example1: Reply to Marta about the Q4 deck
drafts.example2: Two versions of a Slack announcement
drafts.name: Drafts
drafts.needs: Nothing extra. The card shows in the web chat.
drafts.never: Never sends anything - you copy the text and send it yourself.

eval_tool_tuning.does: Scores one tool against eval cases that are already judged, and drafts one tuning proposal per failure class: prompt wording, tool parameters, or tool choice.
eval_tool_tuning.example1: Why does search keep missing the total?
eval_tool_tuning.example2: Tune the lookup tool against last week's cases
eval_tool_tuning.name: Eval tool tuning
eval_tool_tuning.needs: A set of judged eval cases, from the failure-learning loop's eval tries.
eval_tool_tuning.never: Never judges an answer itself and never applies a proposal: drafts are for a human to approve.

follow_ups.does: Offers up to three next steps as buttons under an answer, so what to ask next is one click away.
follow_ups.name: Follow-ups
follow_ups.needs: Nothing extra. The buttons show in the web chat, the widget and the hosted page.
follow_ups.never: Never sends anything on its own - a step goes out only when someone clicks it.

guardrails.does: Hides passwords or personal data, or stops a run, when a message or an answer matches a rule you set.
guardrails.example1: Remove card numbers before they reach the model
guardrails.name: Guardrails
guardrails.never: Never changes anything a rule does not match.

harness.does: Keeps a Claude Code or Codex session open in the agent's sandbox and drives it across turns, as the agent's working backend, while you watch each prompt in the chat.
harness.example1: Fix a failing test, then keep prompting the same session for the follow-ups
harness.example2: Read a module and explain how it works, without changing anything
harness.name: Harness
harness.needs: A connection and a provider key in the vault: an Anthropic key or Claude subscription token for Claude Code, an OpenAI key for Codex.
harness.never: A ChatGPT sign-in does not work here yet; Codex runs on an OpenAI API key. Set Human approval to Always ask to also approve each prompt in the chat.

image_generation.does: Creates an image from a description.
image_generation.example1: A header picture for a blog post
image_generation.example2: A rough mock-up of a poster
image_generation.name: Image generation
image_generation.needs: An API key for the image provider in the vault. Each image is billed by that provider.
image_generation.never: Never posts an image anywhere; it appears in the conversation.

knowledge.does: Lets the agent answer from your documents and say which one each answer came from.
knowledge.example1: Answer staff questions from the HR handbook
knowledge.example2: Find the termination clause in the contracts
knowledge.name: Knowledge search
knowledge.needs: A knowledge base with documents, picked in this panel.
knowledge.never: Never searches a knowledge base this agent is not connected to.

media.does: Moves images out of a long conversation's history, so it stays small and cheaper to send.
media.name: Media offload

memory_files.does: Lets the agent keep notes from one conversation to the next, so it does not start from zero.
memory_files.example1: Remember somebody's team and what they work on
memory_files.example2: Keep a running list of open questions
memory_files.name: Memory
memory_files.never: Never shows one person's notes to another. In a group chat the notes belong to the chat.

mirage.does: Mounts the services you choose - a Drive, a GitHub repository, Notion, a database, an SSH server - as folders, so the agent lists, searches and reads them with a shell, and writes where you allow it.
mirage.example1: Find every contract in a Drive folder that mentions a client
mirage.example2: Search a repository and a Notion workspace in one go
mirage.example3: Read a table from your database and summarise it
mirage.name: Mirage (virtual terminal)
mirage.needs: The services' credentials in the vault, or a connected Google account. A deployment installs the terminal with the mirage extra, and an operator allows the hosts of any server you type.
mirage.never: Never writes to a folder you mounted read-only, and asks a person before each write where you said so.

monitor.does: Starts a long-running command - a test watcher, a log tail, a CI poll - and tells the agent about its new output as it appears, so it does not have to poll.
monitor.example1: Run the test watcher and fix each failure as it shows up
monitor.example2: Tail a deploy log and report the first error
monitor.name: Watch a command
monitor.needs: A workspace with a shell, such as the Sandbox capability or a folder on your computer.
monitor.never: Never keeps a command running after the turn ends: every watch stops with the run.

phone_calls.does: Calls your opted-in verified number, reads a spoken report, or transfers this live call to an allowed contact.
phone_calls.example1: Read my morning report over the phone
phone_calls.example2: Hand a public support call to an opted-in colleague
phone_calls.name: Telephone calls
phone_calls.needs: A configured Twilio telephone endpoint; separate contact consent, available budget and time outside quiet hours.
phone_calls.never: Never authenticates an inbound caller from caller ID, dials an arbitrary number, redials an uncertain submission or extends the original call cap.

planning.does: Lets the agent write a checklist for a bigger task and tick off each step, so the person sees its progress.
planning.example1: Prepare a monthly report in five visible steps
planning.name: Planning
planning.never: Never gives the agent permission to do anything; a plan is only a list.

proof_scenario.does: Proves a change with observed evidence: records a reproduction before the fix and after it, and reports which changed files have proof and which do not.
proof_scenario.example2: Prove this fix before I merge it
proof_scenario.name: Proof scenario
proof_scenario.needs: A reproduction of the failure to run before and after the fix.
proof_scenario.never: Never merges, approves, or takes any other action on the change, and never counts a green unit test as proof.

sandbox.does: Gives the agent its own small computer: it creates and edits files and runs code, and the files are still there next time.
sandbox.example1: Clean up a spreadsheet and hand back the result
sandbox.example2: Write a script, run it and fix it until it works
sandbox.example3: Keep a draft report it updates over several days
sandbox.name: Sandbox
sandbox.needs: A stored workspace, a registered sandbox connection, or a paired desktop computer approved in chat.
sandbox.never: Reaches your computer only after you choose and approve it in the desktop app. File changes and commands follow the agent’s approval rules, plus the chosen native access mode.

secret_request.does: Lets the agent ask for a secret it needs but does not have, naming it and what it is for.
secret_request.example1: What is the Acme API key for listing contacts?
secret_request.example2: Which secret should the nightly report use?
secret_request.name: Request a secret
secret_request.never: Never shows the value to the model, the transcript or a log. The card seals it straight into the vault.

skills.does: Lets the agent follow your written how-tos, loading one when the task needs it.
skills.example1: Write a proposal the way your sales team does
skills.example2: Follow the checklist for a new client
skills.name: Skills
skills.needs: Skills, written under Skills and picked in this panel.
skills.never: Never changes a skill; the agent only reads it.

sol_loop.does: Asks one reviewer to judge the work in rounds until it passes: round 1 reviews the whole change, later rounds check only changed code and open findings.
sol_loop.example1: Is this pull request ready to merge?
sol_loop.example2: Review this draft before it goes out
sol_loop.name: Sol-loop
sol_loop.needs: One model profile for the reviewer, pointed at a Sol model.
sol_loop.never: Never substitutes a missing reviewer or invents a verdict: a reviewer that cannot be reached is reported unavailable, and budget end is not approval.

subagents.does: Lets the agent hand part of a job to another agent and use its answer.
subagents.example1: A front-desk agent that passes legal questions to the legal agent
subagents.example2: Research several topics side by side
subagents.name: Subagents
subagents.needs: Other agents, or specialists defined in this panel. Each handover costs what that agent's run costs.
subagents.never: Never gives another agent more access than it already has.

system_reminders.does: Repeats the agent's key instructions during a long task, so it does not drift away from them.
system_reminders.example1: A long research task that has to keep the requested format
system_reminders.name: Instruction reminders
system_reminders.never: Adds no tools; it only repeats the instructions.

text_to_speech.does: Reads a text aloud as an audio clip.
text_to_speech.example1: A voice-over for a product video
text_to_speech.example2: A spoken version of a weekly summary
text_to_speech.name: Text to speech
text_to_speech.needs: An API key for the speech provider in the vault. Each clip is billed by that provider, per character.
text_to_speech.never: Never sends audio anywhere; the clip appears in the conversation.

thinking.does: Lets the model think before it answers - slower and more expensive, but better on problems with several steps.
thinking.example1: Compare three versions of a contract
thinking.example2: Work out a schedule with many constraints
thinking.name: Thinking
thinking.never: Adds no tools; it changes how the model answers.

tool_output_limits.does: Shortens a very large tool result, so it is not sent to the model again with every message.
tool_output_limits.example1: A search that returns a huge spreadsheet
tool_output_limits.name: Tool output limits
tool_output_limits.never: Never changes the data itself, only how much of it the model reads at once.

tool_search.does: Lets an agent with many tools find the right one when it needs it, instead of reading all of them every time.
tool_search.example1: An agent with many enabled capabilities and bound MCP servers
tool_search.name: Tool search
tool_search.never: Never adds a tool; it only hides tools until the agent looks for one.

video_generation.does: Makes a short video from a description, or from an image it starts with.
video_generation.example1: A ten-second teaser for a product launch
video_generation.example2: An animated version of a generated logo
video_generation.name: Video generation
video_generation.needs: An API key for the video provider in the vault. Each clip is billed by that provider, per second.
video_generation.never: Never posts a video anywhere; it appears in the conversation.

visuals.does: Draws in the conversation - a diagram, an architecture map, an explainer with sliders, a 3D scene - live while the agent writes it. A drawing can be saved as an app.
visuals.example1: Our order flow as a diagram
visuals.example2: A 3D model of the warehouse you can turn
visuals.name: Visuals
visuals.needs: Nothing extra. The visual-design skill makes the drawings look designed.
visuals.never: Never reaches the network - a drawing runs sealed off, like an app's page.

web_fetch.does: Lets the agent open a link and read the page.
web_fetch.name: Read web pages
web_fetch.never: Never logs in or fills in a form; it only reads.

web_research.does: Lets the agent search the internet for current information.
web_research.example1: What changed in this regulation this year?
web_research.example2: Find three competitors and their prices
web_research.name: Web search
web_research.needs: Nothing, with DuckDuckGo or Keenable (a Keenable key in the vault is optional). Brave, Exa or Tavily need their API key in the vault.
web_research.never: Never sends your documents to the search engine, only the search words.

workflows.does: Lets the agent start the published workflows it is granted and read what they answer.
workflows.example1: Start the onboarding workflow for a new customer
workflows.example2: Run the monthly report workflow and summarize its result
workflows.name: Workflows
workflows.needs: At least one published workflow granted to the agent.
workflows.never: Never starts a workflow it was not granted, and never changes a workflow.

apps.body: Agents publish reports, dashboards and small tools as Apps people open by link - and update them when the numbers change.
apps.title: Turn answers into apps

browser.body: With the Web browser an agent clicks, fills forms and reads pages behind a sign-in - and you can take over at any moment.
browser.title: Let an agent use a browser

channels.body: Put an agent in Slack, Telegram or Mattermost, and people ask it right in the thread they are already in.
channels.title: Meet your team where it chats

commands.body: Type / in the chat for commands - summarise, explain, start over - or write your own under Settings → Slash commands.
commands.title: Shortcuts with /

knowledge.body: Upload handbooks, contracts or a whole drive, and agents answer from them and show which page each answer came from.
knowledge.title: Answer from your documents

mcp.body: AgenticOS is an MCP server too: connect Claude Code, Codex or Cursor and build agents, run them and read results without leaving them.
mcp.title: Use it from Claude Code or Cursor

mentions.body: In the chat, type @ to hand the agent one of its servers, capabilities, skills or teammates. It shows as a chip, and the agent uses exactly that.
mentions.title: Point the agent with @

routines.body: Routines start an agent every morning, on a webhook or when an email arrives, and send what it found where your team reads it.
routines.title: Run agents on a schedule

sandbox.body: With a Sandbox an agent writes files, runs code and keeps its work between conversations - safely away from your systems.
sandbox.title: Give an agent its own computer

skills.body: Skills are written how-tos - a proposal template, an onboarding checklist - that an agent loads when the task needs it.
skills.title: Teach the way your team works

subagents.body: Give an agent Subagents and it hands parts of a job to colleagues - a researcher, a reviewer - and you watch them talk it through.
subagents.title: Let agents work as a team

discover.title: Discover AgenticOS

They leave the group when the role is taken away. Group memberships added by hand are never removed. Discord users who have not linked their account get nothing.

improvement.knowledgeAddedHint: These answers came before a document covering them was added, so there is nothing left to draft. Ask again to check the agent now finds it.
improvement.knowledgeDraftCost: Drafting a document is billed to the knowledge base, outside this session's limit.
improvement.knowledgeEmbeddingPriceUnavailable: Whether search finds it cannot be tested: its search model has no known price, so a complete cost cannot be quoted. You can still test with temporary context.
improvement.knowledgeEmbeddingUnavailable: Whether search finds it cannot be tested: this knowledge base’s search service is unavailable. You can still test with temporary context.
improvement.knowledgeEstimate: Includes {cost} for sorting the source answers and grouping missing knowledge (estimate). A draft is written only when you ask for one.
improvement.knowledgeInvalidated: The draft changed or was removed. Check the current draft again before using this result.
improvement.knowledgeNotRetrieved: No demonstrated improvement from the draft: search did not return it for every newly fixed answer. The full check keeps the actual answers and grades.

improvement.knowledgeQuote: {count} independent questions · {excluded} left out · up to {cost} (estimate, including asking both versions and re-asking changed answers).
improvement.knowledgeSearchDisabled: These changes turn knowledge search off. Test with temporary context, or enable search and start a new session.
improvement.knowledgeSeparate: We ask the questions again with the draft added. The result is separate from the agent's and publishes nothing.
improvement.knowledgeTitle: Check whether the draft would help
improvement.knowledgeUnmeasurable: Can’t be measured. Choose at least five independent, gradable questions about this topic.
improvement.knowledgeUntracked: Can’t be measured: this older draft did not record all its source questions. Write a new draft before checking it.

kb.addressHint: The root the service answers on. Ollama's OpenAI-compatible root ends in /v1; an OCR server's is its base.
kb.appliesEachFileYou: This applies to each file you add next and is recorded on it. The collection keeps its own settings - every later upload goes back to them.
kb.builtInReadersRegardless: Text, Markdown and Word files use the built-in readers whichever is chosen.
kb.charactersEachPieceRepeats: Characters each piece repeats from the one before it, so a sentence split across a boundary is still findable.
kb.charactersPerEmbeddedPiece: Characters per embedded piece. Smaller pieces match a question more precisely; larger ones carry more of the surrounding argument.
kb.checkingEndpointModels: Asking this endpoint which embedding models it serves…
kb.chunkingFixedHint: A fixed number of characters, structure ignored.
kb.chunkingMarkdownHint: Split on headings, so a chunk stays inside one section.
kb.chunkingRecursiveHint: Split on paragraphs, then sentences, then words - whatever fits.
kb.chunkingSummary: {size, plural, =1 {1 character} other {# characters}}, {overlap, number} overlapping · {strategy}
kb.citedFileGone: This file is no longer in its knowledge base - it was deleted or replaced after it was cited.
kb.collectionsPointingAtItStop: Collections pointing at this server stop indexing or reading pages until they are moved to another one.
kb.configuredOnceUsedAs: Configured once, used in as many knowledge bases as you like. Each copy syncs on its own schedule.
kb.createKbDescription: Upload documents into it once it exists. Agents search it when it is attached to them or picked in chat.
kb.deploymentWideHint: Offered to every organization, and the only kind of server an app-scoped collection may embed through.
kb.describedByModelIndexed: Described by a model and indexed
kb.embeddingEndpointHint: Leave empty for the global OpenRouter API, or enter a regional URL such as https://eu.openrouter.ai/api/v1. EU routing requires an eligible OpenRouter plan; ZDR is configured separately on OpenRouter.
kb.endpointLacksCollectionModel: This endpoint does not serve {model}, the model this collection's vectors were made with. Leave the endpoint empty, or choose one that serves it.
kb.endpointModelsListed: Only the models this endpoint serves are listed.
kb.endpointModelsUnconfirmed: This endpoint could not be asked which models it serves, so every OpenRouter model is listed. A model it does not serve will fail on the first upload.
kb.endpointServesNoModel: This endpoint serves none of the embedding models AgenticOS offers. Leave the endpoint empty, or choose another provider.
kb.everyPageCameBack: Every page came back as empty scaffolding, which is what an unreadable scan looks like. If this file is a scan or a photo, turn on reading scanned pages in the parse options and upload it again.
kb.formatMarkdownHint: Rebuilds headings, tables and lists - what the Markdown chunking strategy splits on.
kb.formatTextHint: Keeps the page's spatial grid, so a table stays aligned but carries no structure.
kb.frozenAtCreationCollection: Frozen at creation: the collection's vectors are produced by this model and cannot be re-indexed under another one later. The key decides whose account pays for embedding.
kb.howFinelyPageRendered: How finely a page is rendered before OCR reads it. Higher recovers faint scans and costs time.
kb.howHardModelThinks: How hard the model thinks before describing an image. A level a provider does not have maps to its closest one.
kb.howLongLiteparseMay: How long LiteParse may spend on one document before it is abandoned.
kb.howVariedEachDescription: How varied each description is. Left alone the parameter is not sent at all, which is not the same as sending zero - reasoning models reject it outright.
kb.ingestionRecordedNote: What this collection was indexed with, recorded when it was created. It cannot be changed - vectors written by two different models are not comparable, so a collection that needs another one is a new collection.
kb.ingestionSettingsDescription: How documents added to <mono>{name}</mono> are read from here on. Nothing already indexed is re-parsed.
kb.integrationSaved: Integration saved - use it in a knowledge base to start syncing
kb.itsCredentialsAreCopied: Its credentials are copied into an independent source. The original stays here for the next knowledge base that needs it.
kb.keyRequiredHere: Embeddings bill this key, and it has to be one for the chosen provider. There is no deployment-wide key to fall back to.
kb.keylessProvider: {provider} takes no key: it is a server on the deployment's own network, and nothing is billed for these embeddings.
kb.knowledgeBasesAlreadyUsing: Knowledge bases already using it keep their own copy - this only removes the one nothing is syncing from.
kb.leftAloneCollectionInherits: Left alone, this collection inherits whatever defaults the deployment is configured with. The values below are the platform's; changing any one of them sends all of them, and they become this collection's until somebody edits them.
kb.liteparseReadsTextLayer: LiteParse reads the text layer first and OCRs a page only when there is nothing there. OCR dominates the cost of a parse, and most documents are born digital. Turn this off to OCR every page regardless.
kb.localServicesHint: Servers on the deployment's own network - an Ollama that embeds, an OCR sidecar for LiteParse - registered once and chosen per collection. Nothing sent to one leaves the deployment.
kb.modelIsFixed: Model, fixed by the vectors already stored
kb.modelsUnreadable: The list of providers could not be read, so no provider or key can be chosen. Creating this collection will be refused until it can.
kb.name: Name
kb.nextUploadsTitle: How the next uploads are read and filed
kb.noConnectorsAvailable: No source connectors are available. An administrator can enable a connector for this deployment.
kb.noLocalServicesYet: Nothing here yet. Register an Ollama or an OCR server to keep embeddings and OCR on your own network.
kb.notDescribedPictureTable: Not described - a picture of a table is not searchable
kb.nothingHereYetAdd: Nothing here yet. Add one to connect a source before you know which knowledge bases will need it.
kb.nothingIndexedDocumentIts: Nothing is indexed for this document. Its vectors may have been removed since it was ingested.
kb.nothingReadableCameOut: Nothing readable came out of this parse
kb.ocrLanguageHint: Tesseract codes, which are three letters: “eng”, “pol”, “deu”. Join several with “+”.
kb.ocrServerHint: Where LiteParse sends pages to be read. The built-in Tesseract runs inside the worker.
kb.onlyOcrPagesNeed: Only OCR the pages that need it
kb.organizationalUnitDetail: Recorded on each file you add next, so a search can be narrowed to it. Leave it empty to file them under nothing.
kb.overlapRepeats: adjacent chunks repeat their overlap, so boundary text appears twice
kb.pageParsedNothingReadable: This page parsed to nothing readable - likely an unreadable scan.
kb.pagePictureTextCarries: A page that is a picture of text carries no text to extract. PyMuPDF hands such a page to the image model; LiteParse runs its own OCR.
kb.parserLiteparseHint: Local, with its own OCR. Also reads spreadsheets, slide decks and images.
kb.parserLlamaparseHint: A hosted service that reconstructs layout, tables and columns. Billed per page.
kb.parserPymupdfHint: Local and fast. Reads the text a PDF already carries.
kb.problemOcrLanguage: Tesseract codes are three letters - "eng", not "en". Join several with "+", as in "eng+pol".
kb.problemOverlapTooLarge: Must be smaller than the chunk size of {size}.
kb.problemTimeoutRange: More than 0 and at most {max} seconds.
kb.providerMoveKeepsTheIndex: The same model served from somewhere else is the same model, so nothing already indexed changes - the next request just goes to the new provider, on the new key.
kb.registeringNeedsPermission: Registering a server needs the connections permission. Ask an administrator to add one.
kb.sendPicturesInsideDocument: Send the pictures inside a document to a model and index what it says about them. Needs a model profile with a working key, which is checked when this is saved.
kb.serverOnDeploymentNetwork: Registered for this organization. The address has to be reachable from the worker.
kb.tierAgenticHint: Reads structure the way a person would.
kb.tierAgenticPlusHint: The most thorough, and the dearest.
kb.tierFastHint: Cheapest, and the least faithful to layout.
kb.whatModelAskedSay: What the model is asked to say about each image. What it answers is what a search matches, so name the things worth finding.
kb.whereLiteparseStopsWhat: Where LiteParse stops. This is what bounds the cost of one document - the timeout only bounds the wait.
kb.whoseAccountEachParse: Whose account each parse is billed to.
kb.widthIsFixed: The width comes with the model, and the collection is created at it.

pl.accountResponsibility: Odpowiadasz za bezpieczeństwo swoich danych logowania oraz za działania wykonane na Twoim koncie. Powiadom nas na <mail>security@example.com</mail> jeśli podejrzewasz, że konto zostało skompromitowane.
pl.aiOutputDisclaimer: Output AI może zawierać nieścisłości. Nie polegaj na Usłudze dla porad w dziedzinach, gdzie błędy mają realne konsekwencje (medyczne, prawne, finansowe) bez niezależnej weryfikacji.
pl.amaPrawoLubNarusza: łamać prawo lub naruszać praw osób trzecich;
pl.byObsUgiwaUtrzymywa: by obsługiwać, utrzymywać i ulepszać Usługę;
pl.byPrzetwarzaSubskrypcjeI: by przetwarzać subskrypcje i zapobiegać oszustwom;
pl.byWykrywaNaduYcia: by wykrywać nadużycia i egzekwować nasz Regulamin.
pl.byWysyEmaileTransakcyjne: by wysyłać emaile transakcyjne (konto, płatności, alerty bezpieczeństwa);
pl.cieKiRequestW: - ścieżki requestów, czasy odpowiedzi, użycie funkcji, stack traces błędów.
pl.contactQuestions: Pytania? Napisz na <mail>legal@example.com</mail>. Odpowiadamy w ciągu pięciu dni roboczych dla korespondencji prawnej.
pl.gdyKorzystaszZFunkcji: Gdy korzystasz z funkcji AI, Twoje prompty i odpowiedni kontekst są wysyłane do skonfigurowanych dostawców modeli (np. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) w celu przetwarzania. Wybieramy dostawców, którzy umownie zgadzają się nie używać Twoich danych do treningu.
pl.generowaTreCiNielegalnych: generować treści nielegalnych, szkodliwych dla nieletnich, oszukańczych lub wprowadzających w błąd;
pl.hostujemyGWnieW: Hostujemy głównie w UE. Tam, gdzie dane są przetwarzane poza Twoim krajem, opieramy się na standardowych klauzulach umownych lub równoważnych zabezpieczeniach.
pl.imiEmailZhashowaneHas: - imię, email, zhashowane hasło, opcjonalny avatar.
pl.jeLiKorzystaszZ: Jeśli korzystasz z Usługi w imieniu organizacji, akceptujesz Regulamin w jej imieniu i potwierdzasz, że masz do tego upoważnienie.
pl.jeLiWymagaTego: jeśli wymaga tego prawo, ale walczymy gdzie możemy i powiadamiamy dotkniętych użytkowników gdzie jest to prawnie dozwolone.
pl.jesteWCicielemTego: Jesteś właścicielem tego, co wprowadzasz - promptów, dokumentów, treści rozmów („Dane Klienta”). Udzielasz nam ograniczonej licencji na hostowanie, przetwarzanie i wyświetlanie Danych Klienta wyłącznie w celu obsługi Usługi dla Ciebie.
pl.kredytyWygasajNaKo: Kredyty wygasają na końcu każdego cyklu rozliczeniowego. Top-upy pay-as-you-go nie wygasają. Podatki są naliczane gdzie ma to zastosowanie.
pl.maYPlikKt: Mały plik, który Twoja przeglądarka przechowuje na urządzeniu gdy odwiedzasz stronę. Cookies pozwalają nam utrzymywać Cię zalogowanego, pamiętać preferencje i rozumieć jak używane są funkcje.
pl.moEmyAktualizowaTen: Możemy aktualizować ten Regulamin gdy Usługa ewoluuje. Materialne zmiany ogłosimy emailem lub w aplikacji co najmniej 30 dni przed wejściem w życie. Dalsze korzystanie po dacie wejścia w życie oznacza akceptację.
pl.moEszPrzestaKorzysta: Możesz przestać korzystać z Usługi w każdej chwili. Możemy zawiesić lub zakończyć Twój dostęp jeśli naruszysz Regulamin lub z powodów bezpieczeństwa. Sekcje, które powinny przetrwać wypowiedzenie (IP, wyłączenia odpowiedzialności, ograniczenia odpowiedzialności, rozstrzyganie sporów) przetrwają.
pl.moEszTeBlokowa: Możesz też blokować cookies w ustawieniach przeglądarki. Uwaga: blokowanie niezbędnych cookies zepsuje części Usługi (np. nie pozostaniesz zalogowany).
pl.moEszZaakceptowaOdrzuci: Możesz zaakceptować, odrzucić lub dostosować kategorie z bannera cookies pokazywanego przy pierwszej wizycie. Możesz zmienić wybór w każdej chwili z linku w stopce.
pl.nieBDzieszKorzysta: Nie będziesz korzystał z Usługi by:
pl.nieTrenujemyAdnegoZ: Nie trenujemy żadnego z naszych modeli na Twoich danych.
pl.nieTrenujemyNaTwoich: Nie trenujemy na Twoich Danych Klienta.
pl.nieUstawiamyReklamowychCookies: Nie ustawiamy reklamowych cookies. Niektóre osadzone treści (wideo, widgety płatności) mogą ustawiać cookies - podlegają one politykom swoich dostawców.
pl.niniejszyRegulaminPodlegaPrawu: Niniejszy Regulamin podlega prawu jurysdykcji, w której zarejestrowana jest jednostka operacyjna, z wyłączeniem norm kolizyjnych. Spory rozstrzygają sądy tej jurysdykcji, chyba że bezwzględnie obowiązujące prawo stanowi inaczej.
pl.obsUgiwanePrzezNaszego: - obsługiwane przez naszego processora płatności (Stripe). Nigdy nie widzimy numeru Twojej karty.
pl.pamiTajTwojeWybory: Pamiętają Twoje wybory by Usługa nie była powtarzalna. Opcjonalne.
pl.planyPAtneOdnawiaj: Plany płatne odnawiają się automatycznie do momentu anulowania. Opłaty są bezzwrotne, z wyjątkiem przypadków wymaganych prawem. Możesz anulować w każdej chwili - Twój plan pozostaje aktywny do końca bieżącego okresu rozliczeniowego.
pl.pomagajNamZrozumieJak: Pomagają nam zrozumieć jak używana jest Usługa, żebyśmy mogli ją ulepszać. Anonimizujemy adresy IP i nie udostępniamy ich stronom trzecim do reklamy.
pl.powiadomimyCiWAplikacji: Powiadomimy Cię w aplikacji lub mailem przed wejściem w życie jakichkolwiek istotnych zmian. Dalsze korzystanie po dacie wejścia w życie oznacza akceptację.
pl.privacyIntro: Niniejsza Polityka Prywatności wyjaśnia, jak {appName} („my”, „nas”) zbiera, używa, udostępnia i chroni informacje gdy korzystasz z Usługi.
pl.promptyWgrywaneDokumentyRozmowy: - prompty, wgrywane dokumenty, rozmowy z czatu, zawartość baz wiedzy.
pl.przechowujemyDaneKlientaTak: Przechowujemy Dane Klienta tak długo jak konto jest aktywne. Po usunięciu konta backupy są usuwane w ciągu 30 dni. Logi i metryki są przechowywane do 90 dni dla bezpieczeństwa i analizy operacyjnej.
pl.przeglDarkaOsAdres: - przeglądarka, OS, adres IP (do bezpieczeństwa i rate limitingu).
pl.reverseEngineerowaUsUgi: reverse-engineerować Usługi w celu konkurowania z nami;
pl.serviceDescription: {appName} dostarcza oprogramowanie produktywności wspomagane AI - agentów do chatu, retrieval augmented generation (RAG) oraz powiązane narzędzia developerskie. Funkcje ewoluują na bieżąco; możemy je dodawać, zmieniać lub usuwać.
pl.sondowaSkanowaLubTestowa: sondować, skanować lub testować podatności Usługi bez wcześniejszej pisemnej zgody;
pl.termsIntro: Niniejszy Regulamin („Regulamin”) określa zasady dostępu i korzystania z {appName} („Usługa”). Zakładając konto, uzyskując dostęp do Usługi lub klikając „Zgadzam się”, akceptujesz ten Regulamin.
pl.uYwamyPlikW: Używamy plików cookie i podobnych technologii (zbiorczo „cookies”) do obsługi Usługi i jej ulepszania. Ta strona wyjaśnia, czego używamy i jak to kontrolować.
pl.uYwamyTlsTransit: Używamy TLS in transit, AES-256 in rest, role-based access control oraz audit-logged akcji administracyjnych.
pl.uYwanymDoObs: używanym do obsługi Usługi (hosting, dostawcy modeli, processor płatności, dostawa email, monitoring błędów). Aktualna lista dostępna na życzenie.
pl.usUgaJestDostarczana: Usługa jest dostarczana „tak jak jest”. W maksymalnym zakresie dozwolonym prawem wyłączamy wszelkie gwarancje - wyrażone, dorozumiane, ustawowe - w tym merkantylność, przydatność do określonego celu i nienaruszalność.
pl.usUgaNieJest: Usługa nie jest skierowana do dzieci poniżej 16 roku życia. Świadomie nie zbieramy od nich informacji.
pl.usUgaPolegaNa: Usługa polega na dostawcach zewnętrznych (np. API modeli, procesorzy płatności). Korzystanie z tych funkcji podlega też regulaminom tych dostawców. Nie kontrolujemy ich i nie odpowiadamy za ich działania.
pl.wPrzypadkuFuzjiLub: w przypadku fuzji lub sprzedaży, z zachowaniem zobowiązań tej Polityki.
pl.wZakresieDozwolonymPrawem: W zakresie dozwolonym prawem nasza łączna odpowiedzialność za jakiekolwiek roszczenie wynikające lub związane z Usługą nie przekroczy większej z (a) kwoty, którą nam zapłaciłeś w ciągu 12 miesięcy przed roszczeniem lub (b) 100 USD. Żadna ze stron nie odpowiada za szkody pośrednie, przypadkowe, wynikowe lub karne.
pl.wymaganeDoDziaAnia: Wymagane do działania Usługi. Nie można ich wyłączyć. Przykłady: token sesji, token CSRF, preferowany motyw.
pl.yourRightsDescription: W zależności od miejsca zamieszkania, możesz mieć prawo do dostępu, sprostowania, usunięcia lub eksportu swoich danych osobowych, a także do sprzeciwu lub ograniczenia określonego przetwarzania. Napisz na <mail>privacy@example.com</mail> by je zrealizować. Odpowiadamy w ciągu 30 dni.
pl.zachowujemyWszystkiePrawaDo: Zachowujemy wszystkie prawa do Usługi, w tym oprogramowania, designu i znaków towarowych. Ty zachowujesz wszystkie prawa do swoich Danych Klienta i do output'u, który generujesz za pomocą Usługi, z zastrzeżeniem regulaminów dostawców modeli.
pl.zakCaKorzystaniaZ: zakłócać korzystania z Usługi przez innych klientów.

legal.termsIntro: These Terms of Service (“Terms”) govern your access to and use of {appName} (the “Service”). By creating an account, accessing the Service, or clicking “I agree,” you accept these Terms.
legal.theseTermsAreGoverned: These Terms are governed by the laws of the jurisdiction in which the operating entity is registered, excluding conflict-of-law rules. Disputes go to the courts of that jurisdiction unless required otherwise by mandatory law.
legal.weAposLlNotify: We'll notify you in-app or via email before any material change takes effect. Continued use after the effective date constitutes acceptance.
legal.weDoNotTrainOnCustomerData: We don't train on your Customer Data. Period.
legal.weDonAposT: We don't set advertising cookies. Some embedded content (videos, payment widgets) may set cookies - those are governed by their providers' policies.
legal.weDonAposT2: We don't train any of our own models on your data.
legal.weHostPrimarilyEu: We host primarily in the EU. Where data is processed outside your country, we rely on standard contractual clauses or equivalent safeguards.
legal.weKeepCustomerData: We keep Customer Data for as long as your account is active. After deletion, backups are purged within 30 days. Logs and metrics are retained up to 90 days for security and operational analysis.
legal.weMayUpdateThese: We may update these Terms when the Service evolves. Material changes will be announced via email or in-app at least 30 days before they take effect. Continued use after the effective date constitutes acceptance.
legal.weRetainAllRights: We retain all rights to the Service, including software, designs, and trademarks. You retain all rights to your Customer Data and any output you generate using the Service, subject to applicable model providers' terms.
legal.weUseCookiesSimilar: We use cookies and similar technologies (collectively, “cookies”) to operate the Service and improve it. This page explains what we use and how to control it.
legal.weUseOperateService: we use to operate the Service (hosting, model providers, payment processor, email delivery, error monitoring). A current list is available on request.
legal.weUseTlsTransit: We use TLS in transit, AES-256 at rest, role-based access control, and audit-logged admin actions.
legal.whenYouUseAi: When you use AI features, your prompts and the relevant context are sent to our configured model providers (e.g. OpenAI, Anthropic, Google) for processing. We choose providers that contractually agree not to use your data for training.
legal.youCanAcceptReject: You can accept, reject, or customize categories from the cookie banner shown on first visit. You can change your choice anytime from the link in the footer.
legal.youCanAlsoBlock: You can also block cookies in your browser settings. Note: blocking essential cookies will break parts of the Service (e.g. you won't stay logged in).
legal.youCanStopUsing: You can stop using the Service at any time. We may suspend or terminate your access if you breach these Terms or for security reasons. Sections that should survive termination (IP, disclaimers, limitations of liability, dispute resolution) survive.
legal.youOwnWhatYou: You own what you put in - prompts, documents, chat content (“Customer Data”). You grant us a limited license to host, process, and display Customer Data only to operate the Service for you.
legal.youWonAposT: You won't use the Service to:
legal.yourResponseCookieBanner: - your response to the cookie banner.
legal.yourRightsDescription: Depending on where you live, you may have rights to access, correct, delete, or export your personal data, and to object to or restrict certain processing. Email <mail>privacy@example.com</mail> to exercise them. We respond within 30 days.
