mcp.whoCanUseHint: Everyone who manages MCP servers sees and binds it, unless you limit it to groups or people. An agent bound to it keeps working for everyone who may run that agent.
mcp.whoeverSignsGrantsIf: Whoever signs in grants it. If their access at the provider is revoked, this server stops working for every agent until somebody signs in again - so use an account the organization controls.
mcp.yourChatAndDirectMessages: Yours alone - your chat, and your direct messages in a channel.
mcp.yoursAloneYourOwn: Only you. Used in your chats, and by agents set up to act as each person, with your own access.

mcpConnect.browserHint: The client opens this console, you choose the organization and what it may do, and its access renews itself. Connected clients are listed below.
mcpConnect.docs: What the MCP server can do
mcpConnect.keyHint: For a client that cannot open a browser. Create a key above and set it as AGENTICOS_API_KEY in the client’s environment.

claude-code.browser: Run this, then type /mcp in Claude Code and choose agenticos to sign in.
claude-code.key: Run this with AGENTICOS_API_KEY set in your shell.

claude-desktop.browser: In Claude (desktop or claude.ai), open Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector, name it AgenticOS and paste the server URL. Claude signs in through this console. The URL has to be reachable from the internet over HTTPS.
claude-desktop.key: Claude’s connectors always sign in through the browser, so an API key is not used here. Switch to “Through the browser”.

codex.browser: The second command opens the browser to sign in.
codex.key: Codex reads the key from AGENTICOS_API_KEY in its environment.

cursor.browser: Add this to .cursor/mcp.json in your home folder; Cursor asks you to sign in the first time.
cursor.key: Add this to .cursor/mcp.json in your home folder and replace aos_… with your key.

vscode.browser: Add this to .vscode/mcp.json in your project; VS Code asks you to sign in the first time.
vscode.key: Add this to .vscode/mcp.json in your project; VS Code asks for the key once and stores it securely.

mcpConnect.title: Connect an MCP client
mcpConnect.why: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or any other MCP client can work in this organization through AgenticOS's own MCP server: list and run agents, read runs and what they cost, search and fill knowledge bases, invite members.

mcpOauth.connectedWhy: Applications you signed in to with this account, such as Claude Code. Each acts as you, within what you allowed.
mcpOauth.disconnectWhy: Its access ends now, with every token it holds. It has to ask again to reconnect.
mcpOauth.emptyWhy: Add AgenticOS to Claude Code or another MCP client and sign in; it appears here.
mcpOauth.expiredWhy: Start the connection again from the application that sent you here.
mcpOauth.revokeLater: You can disconnect it at any time under Settings → API keys.
mcpOauth.title: {client} wants to act as you
mcpOauth.why: It will use your permissions in the organization below, limited to what you allow. Whatever you choose, you go back to {host}.

memory.clearBody: Deletes every note this agent has written, for every person and every group chat it has talked to. Nothing brings them back.
memory.clearConfirm: This agent will lose everything it has written down. Its conversations are untouched.
memory.clearedToast: {count, plural, =0 {There was nothing to clear} =1 {1 item deleted} other {# items deleted}}
memory.forgetBody: Every agent in this organization forgets what it has written down about you - in this deployment. Your conversations stay; only what agents noted about you goes.
memory.forgetConfirm: Every agent in this organization will forget what it noted about you. Your conversations are untouched.
memory.forgetMemberConfirm: Every agent in this organization will forget what it noted about {name}. Their conversations are untouched.
memory.forgottenToast: {count, plural, =0 {There was nothing to forget} =1 {1 item forgotten} other {# items forgotten}}

mirage.foldersDetail: Add an integration for each source, then choose its service, credentials and access. Each integration becomes a folder the agent can list, search and read.
mirage.jsonHint: Edit as JSON. Valid changes are saved; incomplete JSON keeps the last valid value.
mirage.jsonInvalid: Enter valid JSON of the required type. The last valid value is unchanged.

mirage.notInstalled: This deployment does not have the virtual terminal installed. An operator installs it with the mirage extra.
mirage.organizationAccountsDetail: Everybody who talks to the agent reads this account. The organization connects accounts in the <link>vault</link>.
mirage.personalAccountsDetail: Each person who talks to the agent sees their own accounts, one folder per account. They connect them in the <link>vault</link>.

activity.callAsking: It is asking you something - tap to answer.
activity.callBody: Tap to go back to the call.
activity.questionBody: Tap to answer it in AgenticOS.
activity.runBody: Tap to follow it in AgenticOS.

addPhone.expiresIn: {seconds, plural, =1 {Works for 1 more second} other {Works for # more seconds}}

addPhone.qrLabel: A code that signs the AgenticOS app in as you

addPhone.step2: Choose Scan a code, or point the phone's camera here.
addPhone.step3: Scan the code and confirm your account on the phone.

pair.confirmHint: Continue only if this is your account. Confirming replaces the account signed in on this device.
pair.failedHint: Codes work once, for a minute. Show a new one in the console, under Settings, Mobile app, and scan it again.

settings.heading: Mobile app

setup.contextPermissions: Camera access is requested only when you scan a code. Microphone access is requested when you start voice. Nothing is recorded by these checks.

setup.lockHint: Use Face ID, fingerprint or the device passcode when returning to the app.

setup.testHint: A successful test means a push service accepted it, not that this phone displayed it. Check the notification shade or lock screen.

setup.welcome: Review this connection, even if you already use AgenticOS elsewhere. You can finish optional settings later.

notificationRoutes.title: Private chat notifications
notificationRoutes.unavailable: Destination unavailable — choose again or turn off

onboarding.chooseRole: What do you do? Your agents will know.
onboarding.helpReminder: You can replay any page's tips whenever you like - just click the ? in its header.

connect-app.body: Choose a useful starting task, authorize one app, and ask your assistant to use it. You can skip any step.
connect-app.title: Connect an app?

connect-personal-model.body: Connect your Claude subscription or a personal API key, then choose a model for your signed-in agent runs. Saving a connection or model does not send an inference request.
connect-personal-model.title: Connect a personal model?

create-agent.body: An agent is instructions, a model and a set of tools. Want to build your first one together? We'll check what your organization already has and only stop where you need to.
create-agent.title: Create your first agent?

create-agent-message.body: One agent can write directly to another, in a thread you can read. Shall we send one now? We'll walk you through it and watch the thread appear.
create-agent-message.title: Send a first message between agents?

create-dataset.body: A dataset holds the questions your agents are tested on. Want to make your first one and write a first good case together? We'll walk you through it.
create-dataset.title: Create a dataset?

create-group.body: A group lets you share an agent, a skill or a collection with several people in one step. Want to create one now? We'll walk you through it.
create-group.title: Create a group?

create-kb.body: A knowledge base lets your agents search your documents. Want to set one up now? We'll walk you through it.
create-kb.title: Create a knowledge base?

create-mcp.body: MCP servers give agents tools from other systems. Want to add a connection now? We'll walk you through it.
create-mcp.title: Connect an MCP server?

create-org.body: An organization is a separate space with its own agents, members and settings. Want to create one now? We'll walk you through it.
create-org.title: Create an organization?

create-project-tracker.body: Review an editable published agent and its accounts, then explicitly publish a private tracker with a task table and scheduled checks.
create-project-tracker.title: Set up a project tracker?

create-routine.body: A routine runs an agent with nobody at the keyboard - on a schedule, or when an event arrives. Want to set one up now? We'll walk you through it and fire the first run together.
create-routine.title: Set up your first routine?

create-skill.body: Skills are reusable instructions you can attach to any agent. Want to make your first one now? We'll walk you through it.
create-skill.title: Create a skill?

create-workflow.body: A workflow chains steps into an automation your agents run. Want to start one now? We'll open the create dialog so you can pick a blank canvas or a template.
create-workflow.title: Build a workflow?

explore-chat.body: See how to start a conversation, switch which agent answers, and change the model or thinking effort for a single chat. Want a quick guided run through it?
explore-chat.title: Take a quick tour of chat?

first-improvement.body: We’ll read what went wrong, then stop for you to look. Writing changes and testing them each wait for you to press Next step, and each is priced first. Nothing goes live until you accept and publish it.
first-improvement.title: Improve

first-skill-improvement.body: See who the change is checked on and what it costs before anything runs. Nothing changes in the skill until you accept it.
first-skill-improvement.title: Improve this skill

improvement-session.body: See what each step did: the questions, today's answers, the result, and what publishing changes where people use the agent.
improvement-session.title: Walk through this session

skill-improvement-session.body: See the steps, each agent's result, and what you may do with the change.
skill-improvement-session.title: Walk through this session

test-change.body: Run the draft against the live version on a dataset and read the verdict: which cases broke, which were fixed, and whether it is worth publishing. We'll walk you through it.
test-change.title: Test a change before it goes live?

onboarding.saveFailed: We couldn't save that you've seen the walkthrough, so it may show again next time.

activity-approvals.body: Runs that paused for a human decision queue here. Approve or reject each one and the run picks up from where it stopped - this tab only appears if you're allowed to decide them.
activity-approvals.title: What's waiting on you

activity-overview.body: Every run is recorded with its cost and outcome, so you can see what your agents did and step in when one is waiting on a decision. These figures summarise the lot.
activity-overview.title: Watch activity

activity-runs.body: The full history: who ran which agent, what it cost and how it ended. Filter it, or open a run to see the whole conversation and the tools it called.
activity-runs.title: Every run

activity-spend.body: Spend over time and by agent, against the budgets you've set - so an agent quietly getting expensive shows up here before the bill does.
activity-spend.title: Where the money went

agent-assistant-strip.body: Review proposed changes in Evals, check them against a dataset, and accept each one into the draft. Start Improve from the Evals toolbar.
agent-assistant-strip.title: Suggestions

agent-availability.body: Availability is where a published agent goes live - a web chat, an embed on your site, Slack or Telegram - and where you decide who to share it with.
agent-availability.title: Put it to work

agent-editor-fullscreen.body: Use the expand button to read or edit the whole document. Closing the expanded editor keeps your current draft.
agent-editor-fullscreen.title: Expand the editor

agent-environment-guards.body: Name the eval suites an environment needs to pass on a version before it takes it. A version that has not passed them is held back, and an override needs a reason and the permission to give one.
agent-environment-guards.title: Guards

agent-eval-suites.body: Hold the agent to a dataset without remembering to: run it every night, on every publish or promotion, or when a skill, knowledge base or context file it reads changes. You are told when a case breaks.
agent-eval-suites.title: Suites

agent-evals.body: Run the agent over a dataset to see which cases it passes, what it costs, and whether a change made it better or worse than the version before.
agent-evals.title: Evals

agent-failure-learning.body: The failures this agent keeps repeating, mined from its real runs. Track a pattern into the ledger, prove a fix with an eval case, and apply it once the gate passes.
agent-failure-learning.title: Learn from what went wrong

agent-gaps.body: The questions this agent searched a knowledge base for and found nothing. Each one links to the run it came from.
agent-gaps.title: What it went looking for

agent-history.body: Each publish freezes the spec as a version you can promote to an environment, roll back to, or read the run history against.
agent-history.title: Every version, kept

agent-identity.body: The name is what people pick in chat and find in the catalog. A duplicate starts as its source with a suffix, so rename it here; the handle other agents reach it by stays the same.
agent-identity.title: Call it something recognizable

agent-improvement-history.body: Each Improve session the agent had: what it measured, what was decided and what it cost. A finished one opens to be read.
agent-improvement-history.title: Every improvement, on record

agent-instructions.body: Open an agent and you land in the Builder, where it's assembled tab by tab. Build comes first: the instructions are its behaviour, written in plain Markdown rather than code.
agent-instructions.title: Instructions are the behaviour

agent-knowledge.body: Knowledge lets the agent search the collections you pick, so it answers from your own material instead of guessing from training alone.
agent-knowledge.title: Point it at your docs

agent-limits.body: Cap the monthly spend and the steps a single run may take, and choose who gets told when the agent hits a limit or fails.
agent-limits.title: Keep it in bounds

agent-mcp.body: Below the capabilities, attach MCP servers - ready-made tool sets like GitHub or Slack, connected once for the organization and reused across agents.
agent-mcp.title: And whole tool sets

agent-messages.body: When one agent writes to another, the thread lands here, most recently active first. Open a thread to read it, reply as either of its agents, or react to a message.
agent-messages.title: Messages between agents

agent-model.body: The model underneath does the reasoning. Swap it, dial how hard it thinks, or turn on step-by-step reasoning - all without touching the instructions above.
agent-model.title: Choose the brain

agent-publish.body: Nothing runs until you publish. Publishing freezes the current draft as a version, and that version is what answers everywhere the agent is available.
agent-publish.title: Publish to ship it

agent-share.body: Add a person or a group and choose what they can do, or open it to the whole organization. The owner always keeps access.
agent-share.title: Share it

agent-skills.body: Skills are written know-how the agent reads before it acts - a procedure, a house style, a checklist - and the same one can be shared across agents.
agent-skills.title: Hand it a playbook

agent-starters.body: What the chat offers somebody opening this agent with nothing said yet. A newcomer learns what the agent is for from these more than from its description, so make each one a real question it answers well.
agent-starters.title: First messages

agent-system-knowledge.body: Switch on a search of the knowledge bases the platform hands each run - the graded agent's, the gap's, the ones cases are drafted from - and cap how many paid steps it may take.
agent-system-knowledge.title: Knowledge base

agent-system-toolbox.body: A system agent reaches nothing past its prompt, so its Toolbox holds only what it reads while it works. Files and skills are offered only when shared with the whole organization, because the platform runs it for everyone.
agent-system-toolbox.title: What it reads

agent-test.body: Opens a chat beside the Builder that answers as your unpublished draft, or as any environment. Test runs are counted and budgeted, and marked in Activity.
agent-test.title: Try it as you build

agent-test-connections.body: A named environment can answer the agent's MCP servers and vault keys with test ones - a sandbox CRM, a test mailbox. Evals run there, and a tool that writes with no test connection is held and recorded instead of run.
agent-test-connections.title: Test connections

agent-test-draft.body: Before you publish, run the draft against the live version on a dataset. The verdict says whether the change made the agent better or worse.
agent-test-draft.title: Test the draft

agent-toolbox.body: The Toolbox is what an agent can actually do. Switch on built-in capabilities like web search, code or files, and each becomes a tool the model may call mid-answer.
agent-toolbox.title: Give it tools

agent-voice.body: Take calls with a realtime model and voice on the Voice calls tab, and on the Dictation tab choose whether the chat microphone uses a provider or the browser.
agent-voice.title: Voice

agents-filters.body: Filter by status or search by name once the roster grows past a screenful.
agents-filters.title: Find one fast

agents-new.body: An agent is its instructions, a model, and the tools, MCP servers and skills you give it. Create one here, then publish a version so it runs the same way everywhere - chat, API, Slack or a widget.
agents-new.title: Build an agent

agents-system.body: The agents the platform runs itself, grouped by what they do: the judges that grade eval answers, the case generator, the gap drafter and classifier, and the authoring assistant. Open one to change its instructions, model or budget; a dataset picks its judge on its Grading tab, and New agent adds another judge.
agents-system.title: System agents

agents-templates.body: Twenty-eight ready-made agents by industry. Installing one creates a draft with its skills already bound.
agents-templates.title: Start from a template

app-connections.body: Start with a goal and connect only the apps you need. Each provider asks for its own authorization. The MCP servers tab includes custom servers; More has channels, remote agents, the vault and sandboxes.
app-connections.title: Connect your apps

artifact-actions.body: If the page can run workflows, they're listed here with a link to their runs. The page can only ask: each run waits for you to confirm it, runs as you, and shows what it will send.
artifact-actions.title: Workflows this page can run

artifact-change-owner.body: A page's data is read with its owner's access. Change owner gives the page to another member right away, and its data stays hidden until the new owner confirms it.
artifact-change-owner.title: Change owner

artifact-consent.body: When a page shows live table data, its owner decides who else sees it. Until then, this notice says what others see. Confirm data shows exactly what is shared, and with whom, before you agree.
artifact-consent.title: Confirming a page's data

artifact-public-data.body: The data this page shows changed, so its public link shows none until it's confirmed again. Confirm data shows what the link would share, and with whom.
artifact-public-data.title: Confirm public data again

artifact-requests.body: Requests about this page wait here: someone asking to open it or share it more widely, or an editor's version that shows different data. Review compares it with the version others see now.
artifact-requests.title: Requests

artifact-review.body: An editor published a version that shows different data. Review data change compares it with the version others see now and marks anything new. Approve shares it; Decline keeps the earlier version.
artifact-review.title: Reviewing a data change

artifact-strip.body: The page's name, who can open it, and Share. When the page needs something from you, like data to confirm or a request to answer, it shows up here.
artifact-strip.title: This page

artifacts-groups.body: Narrow the list to what one group was given. A group is who something reaches, so it is also how the list is grouped.
artifacts-groups.title: By department

artifacts-list.body: Reports and dashboards your agents published. Open one to see it, pick an earlier version, share it with colleagues or give it a public link.
artifacts-list.title: Published pages

assistant-agent-picker.body: Select a published agent you can run. The next question goes to that agent, while previous answers keep their original attribution.
assistant-agent-picker.title: Choose who answers

assistant-page-context.body: The next question includes the page details shown here. View them before sending or switch page context off. Queued questions keep the page and agent selected when you submitted them.
assistant-page-context.title: Include the current page

assistant-widget.body: Open the floating assistant to ask about the page you are viewing. Choose who answers, inspect or switch off the page context, and keep asking as you navigate. Its speech bubbles suggest what to do on each page.
assistant-widget.title: Your Architect

channels-discord-roles.body: Map a role in a Discord server to a group here. Linked members who hold the role join the group, and leave it when the role is taken away.
channels-discord-roles.title: Discord roles

channels-list.body: The platforms this organization is reachable on. A channel belongs to the organization, not one agent, so the same bot can serve every agent bound to it.
channels-list.title: Connected channels

channels-new.body: Register a chat platform - Slack, Telegram, Mattermost - and any agent can be bound to answer there. The bot's token is sealed in the vault. Add one here.
channels-new.title: Reach agents where people are

channels-phone.body: Choose a Twilio SMS bot, a public voice exposure for inbound calls, limits and authorized transfer contacts. Copy the webhook URLs into Twilio. Member phone consent is separate.
channels-phone.title: Set up telephone routing

chat-agent-picker.body: Switch between your agents right here. Each brings its own instructions, tools and knowledge, so the same question can get a very different answer.
chat-agent-picker.title: Choose who answers

chat-approval-mode.body: Follow the agent's own settings, ask about every tool it can use, or - if you may decide approvals - let this conversation run without stopping. Every waived call is still recorded against your account.
chat-approval-mode.title: Decide how much you are asked

chat-background-tasks.body: Independent work opens a fresh topic in this project. Keep talking here; the agent returns with the result. Open or stop each task from this strip.
chat-background-tasks.title: Background topics

chat-coding-accounts.body: Connect Codex or Claude Code without leaving the chat. These are your private cloud accounts; local desktop tools keep their own sign-in.
chat-coding-accounts.title: Your coding accounts

chat-coding-revert.body: Open a coding task to review its changed files. Revert this task restores those files only when none has changed since the task ended.
chat-coding-revert.title: Review and revert a coding task

chat-coding-settings.body: Choose a model and reasoning level from the installed coding agent. Choices belong to this conversation; leaving them unset keeps the coding agent’s own settings.
chat-coding-settings.title: Coding model and reasoning

chat-composer.body: Type a message, drop in a file, or start with a slash-command. Enter sends; Shift+Enter adds a line.
chat-composer.title: Ask anything

chat-local-coding.body: Choose Claude Code or Codex on this computer for this conversation, even when the agent has no Coding agent capability. Its existing approval and read-only rules still apply. Each task asks for native confirmation.
chat-local-coding.title: Coding agent

chat-local-skills.body: Choose which sources this conversation may read. Skills stay on your computer; enabled sources settle name clashes in the order .agents, .claude, .codex. AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md provide project instructions. New chats start with every source off.
chat-local-skills.title: Your local skills and instructions

chat-model-picker.body: Pick which of the organization's models answers - just for this conversation, without changing the agent.
chat-model-picker.title: Tune the model

chat-plan.body: An agent that plans keeps a checklist here, above the composer - the step in flight, and how much is left. Open it for the whole plan; it stays current as the run works through it.
chat-plan.title: What it is working to

chat-start.body: New chat opens a fresh thread, and your past conversations stack up in this rail. It's the quickest way to try an agent out and watch how it works, step by step.
chat-start.title: Chat with your agents

chat-subscription-model.body: Choose one of your saved Claude subscription models to power this chat. The connection stays personal; manage it in Settings → AI connections.
chat-subscription-model.title: Use your Claude subscription

chat-visual.body: An agent with Visuals draws diagrams, explainers and 3D scenes here, live while it writes them. Open one full screen, download it, ask about it, or save it as an app with a link you can share.
chat-visual.title: Drawings

chat-voice-call.body: Start a voice call. The agent answers aloud, uses its tools, and asks you before acting; every turn is saved here as text.
chat-voice-call.title: Talk to the agent

chat-your-connections.body: An agent bound to each person's own account speaks to Notion or Jira as you. This lists which of its services need an account of yours, and connects one without leaving the chat.
chat-your-connections.title: Your own accounts, where the agent uses them

claude-subscription-connect.body: Open Claude sign-in, complete it with your own account, and paste the returned code. Once connected, add a subscription model and choose it in an agent or chat.
claude-subscription-connect.title: Connect your Claude subscription

connections-more.body: The More tab holds channels, remote agents, vault and sandbox settings available to your role.
connections-more.title: More connections

context-editor-fullscreen.body: Use the expand button to read or edit the whole document. Closing the expanded editor keeps your current draft.
context-editor-fullscreen.title: Expand the editor

context-groups.body: Narrow the list to what one group was given. A group is who something reaches, so it is also how the list is grouped.
context-groups.title: By department

context-list.body: The context files this organization holds. One file can feed every agent, so a fact you fix here is fixed for all of them at once.
context-list.title: Shared context

context-new.body: Context files are the background every agent carries - company facts, tone, terms - injected into each prompt without you pasting them in every time. Add one here.
context-new.title: Add standing context

dashboard-customize.body: Customize opens an editor: drag a card to move it between sections, drag its edge to resize it from a quarter of the row to the whole width, hide the ones you never read, and Add a widget for the rest of the catalog - the same card more than once if you want it per agent. Sections can be renamed, coloured, collapsed and added to. Save keeps it, Cancel discards it, and Reset to default puts back the arrangement you started with. Layouts holds several of these arrangements and switches between them, so the one you read on a Monday need not be the one you read while something is on fire. All of it is per person - nobody else sees your arrangement.
dashboard-customize.title: Make it your own

dashboard-filters.body: Every number on this page follows the period you pick here, and you can hide sections you don't need. The view lives in the URL, so it survives a reload and travels in a link.
dashboard-filters.title: Slice the dashboard

dataset-grading.body: Choose the checks every answer must pass and the tool calls a case expects. Save the grading changes together at the bottom.
dataset-grading.title: How cases are graded

dataset-judge.body: Choose a saved model with search, or add a model if you have permission. Set the criteria and reference comparison. Older scores keep the grading configuration they used.
dataset-judge.title: The judge

dataset-review.body: All graded answers appear here, including those already reviewed. Filter by outcome, agent or tag, then open an answer to inspect its evidence and record a decision.
dataset-review.title: Review

datasets-add-case.body: A case is a question the agent answers and what a good answer looks like. Every case you add makes a new version of the dataset.
datasets-add-case.title: Write a case

datasets-generate.body: The generator drafts cases from four sources: the agent's instructions and tools, its knowledge base, real chats (production only, never eval runs), and red teaming. You see the estimated cost before anything is spent.
datasets-generate.title: Have cases drafted

datasets-helper-settings.body: Settings groups grading, case generation and agent improvement. Choose their models and instructions here. A running task keeps the settings it started with.
datasets-helper-settings.title: Configure the evaluation helpers

datasets-list.body: Every change to a dataset's cases makes a new version, so an eval run always points at questions that do not move.
datasets-list.title: Your datasets

datasets-new.body: A dataset holds the questions an agent is tested on. Create one here, then add cases by hand, from a file, from an answer rated up or down in chat, or from a turn in Activity.
datasets-new.title: Collect test cases

datasets-proposals.body: Drafted cases wait here. Accept them as they are, edit them first, or dismiss them. One Accept is one new version.
datasets-proposals.title: Decide the drafts

desktop-local-agents.body: Check Claude Code and Codex installation and sign-in here. The desktop app opens their own sign-in commands in your terminal. Choose On this computer in the agent capability and a folder in Work on to run a task locally.
desktop-local-agents.title: Coding agents on this computer

eval-verdict.body: Which side did better, by how many confirmed cases, and the pass rate before and after. From here, see what changed between the versions, open the cases that broke, or publish.
eval-verdict.title: The verdict

evals-all.body: The runs of every agent you may see, newest first. Each opens on its verdict; an agent's Evals tab holds the same runs for that agent alone.
evals-all.title: Every eval run

finish.body: That's the tour. Replay any page's tips anytime from the help button at the top - head to your dashboard whenever you're ready to start building.
finish.title: You're all set

flow-agent-create.body: Choose New agent, give it a name and a short description, and create it. That opens the builder, where the rest of this happens. We'll move on as soon as it's created.
flow-agent-create.title: Name your agent

flow-agent-instructions.body: Tell the agent who it is and what it should do - this is its system prompt. Write a line or two, then choose Next.
flow-agent-instructions.title: Write its instructions

flow-agent-knowledge.body: Attach a knowledge base and the agent can search those documents and cite them. You can skip this and add one anytime - choose Next to move on.
flow-agent-knowledge.title: Give it documents to read (optional)

flow-agent-knowledge-ask.body: A knowledge base lets this agent search your documents and cite them, and you don't have one yet. Want to create one now and attach it? We'll guide you there and all the way back.
flow-agent-knowledge-ask.title: No knowledge base yet - create one?

flow-agent-knowledge-attach.body: Open the Knowledge tab and attach the knowledge base you just created, then choose Next.
flow-agent-knowledge-attach.title: Attach what you made

flow-agent-knowledge-create.body: Choose New knowledge base - the form opens and we'll walk it together, field by field. Afterwards we'll walk you back to your agent.
flow-agent-knowledge-create.title: Create the knowledge base

flow-agent-knowledge-return-edit.body: Choose the edit pencil on the agent you just built to reopen its builder.
flow-agent-knowledge-return-edit.title: Open your agent again

flow-agent-knowledge-return-nav.body: Choose Agents in the sidebar to head back to the agent you were building.
flow-agent-knowledge-return-nav.title: Back to your agents

flow-agent-limits.body: Cap what this agent can spend in a month and how many steps one run may take, and choose who's told when it reaches a limit. It's how an agent that loops or runs away stops itself. Choose Next to move on.
flow-agent-limits.title: Set a budget (optional)

flow-agent-mcp.body: MCP servers give the agent tools from other systems you've connected. Attach any here, or choose Next to move on.
flow-agent-mcp.title: Add MCP servers (optional)

flow-agent-mcp-ask.body: An MCP server gives this agent tools from another system, and you haven't connected one yet. Want to connect one now? It's a quick dialog right here - no leaving the builder, and we'll pick up the moment it's connected.
flow-agent-mcp-ask.title: No MCP server connected - connect one?

flow-agent-mcp-attach.body: Connecting a server doesn't hand it to this agent. Tick the one you just connected so the agent can use its tools, then choose Next.
flow-agent-mcp-attach.title: Give it the server

flow-agent-mcp-connect.body: Choose Connect a server - the catalog opens right here in the builder, and we'll pick one together.
flow-agent-mcp-connect.title: Open the catalog

flow-agent-message-body.body: Say what the other agent needs to hear — up to 16,000 characters.
flow-agent-message-body.title: Write the message

flow-agent-message-create.body: Open the new-message dialog to send one agent's words to another.
flow-agent-message-create.title: Send a first message

flow-agent-message-recipient.body: Search the agents you may message and pick the one this goes to.
flow-agent-message-recipient.title: Pick the recipient

flow-agent-message-send.body: Send the message, then step on to see the new thread.
flow-agent-message-send.title: Send it

flow-agent-message-sender.body: Choose which of your runnable agents sends this message.
flow-agent-message-sender.title: Pick the sending agent

flow-agent-model-add.body: Your organization has no model yet. Pick a provider, name a model, and paste a key - it's stored in the vault and the model is ready. We'll move on once it's added.
flow-agent-model-add.title: Add a model

flow-agent-model-none.body: An agent needs a model to run, and this organization has none. Adding one needs the connections permission you don't have - ask an admin to add a model, then this agent can use it. Choose Next to look at the rest for now.
flow-agent-model-none.title: No model in this organization yet

flow-agent-model-pick.body: Pick the model this agent should run on from the list - an agent needs one to run, so we'll move on once it's set.
flow-agent-model-pick.title: Choose its model

flow-agent-platform-mcp.body: This platform's own server needs no connection: switched on, the agent can answer questions about agents, runs and knowledge here, as whoever it talks to - and asks before changing anything.
flow-agent-platform-mcp.title: Let it act in the platform (optional)

flow-agent-publish.body: An agent has to be published before you can chat with it - a draft can't take messages. Click Publish to make this version live; we'll move on the moment it's published.
flow-agent-publish.title: Publish it

flow-agent-run-pick.body: You're in the chat now. Open the picker and choose the agent you just published, so your first message goes to it.
flow-agent-run-pick.title: Pick your agent

flow-agent-run-send.body: Type a prompt and send it - your agent's first run, and the end of the tour. We'll close the moment it's on its way.
flow-agent-run-send.title: Send it a message

flow-agent-skills.body: A skill is written know-how the agent loads when it's relevant - a refund policy, a house style. Attach any, or choose Next to move on.
flow-agent-skills.title: Give it skills (optional)

flow-agent-skills-ask.body: A skill is written know-how the agent loads when it's relevant, and you don't have one yet. Want to create one now and attach it? We'll guide you there and all the way back.
flow-agent-skills-ask.title: No skills yet - create one?

flow-agent-skills-attach.body: Open the Skills tab and attach the skill you just created, then choose Next.
flow-agent-skills-attach.title: Attach your skill

flow-agent-skills-create.body: Choose New skill - the form opens and we'll walk it together, field by field. Afterwards we'll walk you back to your agent.
flow-agent-skills-create.title: Create the skill

flow-agent-skills-return-edit.body: Choose the edit pencil on the agent you just built to reopen its builder.
flow-agent-skills-return-edit.title: Open your agent again

flow-agent-skills-return-nav.body: Choose Agents in the sidebar to head back to the agent you were building.
flow-agent-skills-return-nav.title: Back to your agents

flow-agent-tools.body: Capabilities let the agent do things - search the web, run code, call another system. Switch on what it needs, or choose Next to move on.
flow-agent-tools.title: Give it tools (optional)

flow-app-authorize.body: Connect an app and review its permissions on the provider's screen. When you return, T3OS verifies the account. Continue to First task, choose the account, and ask your assistant. Finish this guide whenever you are ready; it does not authorize an app.
flow-app-authorize.title: Authorize, then try it

flow-app-goal.body: Pick Prepare my day, Review my inbox, or Find project answers, then choose apps. One connected account is enough to start. You can change the goal or skip setup.
flow-app-goal.title: Choose your first task

flow-chat-agent.body: This picks which of your published agents replies. Open it to switch agents - you can even change partway through a conversation. Choose Next.
flow-chat-agent.title: Choose who answers

flow-chat-composer.body: Write your message here and send it - that's your first conversation. Choose Finish when you're ready.
flow-chat-composer.title: Type and send

flow-chat-controls.body: Open Controls to run this chat on a different model, or change how hard it thinks - just for this conversation, without touching the agent itself. Choose Next.
flow-chat-controls.title: Tune this conversation

flow-chat-needs-agent.body: Chat talks to a published agent, and you don't have one yet. Want to build one first? We'll guide you through it and you can come back to chat after. Or skip to look around chat for now.
flow-chat-needs-agent.title: No published agent to chat with yet

flow-chat-start.body: Choose New conversation to begin a fresh thread. Each one keeps its own history and settings. Choose Next when you've had a look.
flow-chat-start.title: Start a conversation

flow-dataset-add-case.body: Choose Add case. A case is one question, and what a good answer to it looks like.
flow-dataset-add-case.title: Add your first case

flow-dataset-case-answers.body: Write a reference answer or the key facts the response should include. You can use tool expectations or checks instead.
flow-dataset-case-answers.title: What a correct answer contains

flow-dataset-case-checks.body: A check is a rule the answer is scored by, such as that it mentions 30 days. Each one names its type and carries that rule's parameters.
flow-dataset-case-checks.title: Rules about the answer

flow-dataset-case-counter.body: Expand this section to add an answer known to be wrong, such as one rated down in a conversation.
flow-dataset-case-counter.title: An answer to avoid

flow-dataset-case-history.body: Expand this section if the message depends on an earlier conversation. Add its messages in order, oldest first.
flow-dataset-case-history.title: Conversation context

flow-dataset-case-labels.body: Tags group results, such as billing or refusal. The note says why the case exists - what went wrong, or what it guards.
flow-dataset-case-labels.title: Tags and a note

flow-dataset-case-question.body: Write the message the agent should answer, as a real user would phrase it.
flow-dataset-case-question.title: What the agent is asked

flow-dataset-case-save.body: A case has to say what the answer is tested against: a reference answer, a counter-example, a tool call or a check. Until it has one, Save case stays off and says what is missing.
flow-dataset-case-save.title: Save the case

flow-dataset-case-tools.body: List the tools the agent must call, with the arguments that have to match. Choose how they are matched: in any order, in this order with others allowed between, or exactly these and nothing else.
flow-dataset-case-tools.title: The tools it should call

flow-dataset-create.body: Choose New dataset - the form opens and we'll fill it together.
flow-dataset-create.title: Create a dataset

flow-dataset-field-create.body: Choose Create. We'll move on the moment it's saved.
flow-dataset-field-create.title: Create it

flow-dataset-field-name.body: Say what it tests, like refund questions. Then choose Next.
flow-dataset-field-name.title: Name it

flow-dataset-generate.body: Pick an agent and the sources - the agent itself, its knowledge base, real chats or red teaming - and the generator drafts cases for you to review. Nothing reaches the dataset until you accept it.
flow-dataset-generate.title: Or let the generator draft them

flow-dataset-next.body: In Settings, choose how answers are graded. Then run an agent on this dataset and inspect its answers in Results.
flow-dataset-next.title: Next: grading, then an eval

flow-dataset-open.body: It is the first card - the one changed last. Open it to add its first case.
flow-dataset-open.title: Open your dataset

flow-dataset-sources.body: Write them here, or import a CSV or JSONL file from this menu. In chat, rate an answer up or down and add it - a thumbs-up keeps it as the reference, a thumbs-down as the counter-example. In Activity, add any agent turn of a run.
flow-dataset-sources.title: Where the next cases come from

flow-group-create.body: Choose New group, give it a name, and create it. We'll move on as soon as it exists.
flow-group-create.title: Create the group

flow-improvement-accept.body: Publish the new version, or keep the changes as a draft to publish later. Nothing is accepted or published by itself.
flow-improvement-accept.title: Accept

flow-improvement-automatic-check.body: On the first session, tick this to test these questions again whenever the agent changes. A version that breaks one of them waits before it reaches where people use the agent.
flow-improvement-automatic-check.title: Automatic check

flow-improvement-changes.body: The changes the helper wrote. The session stops here: tick the ones to test and correct any wording before they are tested.
flow-improvement-changes.title: Changes

flow-improvement-check.body: Today's version and the changed one answer the same questions in one test. Each bar shows how far each has got, and the result opens once the test is done.
flow-improvement-check.title: Check

flow-improvement-details.body: Adjust the spending limit, inspect the test questions or check today’s answers. The helper’s model and instructions live in the dataset’s Settings.
flow-improvement-details.title: Show details

flow-improvement-guard.body: Each place people use the agent says what publishing does there: it switches at once, switches after its automatic check passes, or stays on its version.
flow-improvement-guard.title: Where people use it

flow-improvement-next-step.body: Each stop ends here: what the next step does and what it costs. Nothing is spent until you press it.
flow-improvement-next-step.title: Next step

flow-improvement-question-set.body: The questions this session will test on: where they come from, and how many help write the changes against how many are kept aside to check them.
flow-improvement-question-set.title: Test questions

flow-improvement-questions.body: The questions each change is tested on, as they were when the session started. Some help write the changes; the rest are kept aside to check the result.
flow-improvement-questions.title: Test questions

flow-improvement-results.body: The verdict says which questions are newly fixed and newly broken, on every question and on those kept aside. Each changed answer shows before and after, with the grader's sentence.
flow-improvement-results.title: Result

flow-improvement-review.body: Doubt a grade? Open the full check and send the answer to Review. A person's decision replaces the grader's, and the result is worked out again.
flow-improvement-review.title: Review

flow-improvement-start.body: We read what went wrong and stop for you to look. You press Next step to write changes, and again to test them; each step is priced before you press. Nothing goes live until you accept it.
flow-improvement-start.title: Improve

flow-improvement-steps.body: Five steps. The session stops after Understand and after Changes for you to look and press Next step; a step opens once it has something to show.
flow-improvement-steps.title: Steps

flow-improvement-test-set.body: The agent's own test questions are already chosen and priced. Start improving is the one decision here; nothing is spent before it.
flow-improvement-test-set.title: Time and cost

flow-improvement-understand.body: What went wrong, sorted into what the agent can fix and what the knowledge base is missing. Answers the classifier found nothing wrong with are listed apart, as not a problem to fix. There is nothing to set here: the session stops so you can read it before the next step.
flow-improvement-understand.title: Understand

flow-kb-create.body: Choose New knowledge base - the form opens and we'll walk it together, field by field.
flow-kb-create.title: Create the knowledge base

flow-kb-field-create.body: Choose Create. We'll move on the moment it exists - you'll add documents to it right after.
flow-kb-field-create.title: Create it

flow-kb-field-embeddings.body: How documents are indexed for search. It's frozen at creation, but the deployment default is right for almost everyone - expand it only if you know you need a different model. Choose Next.
flow-kb-field-embeddings.title: Embeddings (leave the default)

flow-kb-field-name.body: Name it after what it will hold - Product docs, Support wiki - so anyone attaching it to an agent knows what they're giving it. Then choose Next.
flow-kb-field-name.title: Name it

flow-kb-field-scope.body: Personal is yours alone; Organization makes it available to every member and agent. For a base your agents will search, pick Organization. Then choose Next.
flow-kb-field-scope.title: Choose who it belongs to

flow-mcp-field-connect.body: Choose Connect. We check the server answers and move on the moment it's connected - a server that signs in through the provider will hand off to their consent screen instead.
flow-mcp-field-connect.title: Connect it

flow-mcp-field-form.body: Name it - the name prefixes its tool names - keep Organization so your agents can use it, and paste a token if this server asks for one. Then choose Next.
flow-mcp-field-form.title: Fill in the connection

flow-mcp-field-pick.body: This is the catalog of systems your agents can get tools from. Find the one you want and choose Connect on it.
flow-mcp-field-pick.title: Pick a server

flow-org-create.body: Choose New organization, give it a name, and create it. We'll move on as soon as it exists.
flow-org-create.title: Create the organization

flow-personal-model-connect.body: Connect Claude by opening its sign-in page and pasting the returned code, or save an Anthropic or OpenAI API key. Then add a model and select it in an agent or chat. Setup does not send an inference request.
flow-personal-model-connect.title: Connect and choose a model

flow-project-tracker-create.body: Review an editable published agent and its accounts, then explicitly publish a private tracker with a task table and scheduled checks.
flow-project-tracker-create.title: Set up a project tracker?

flow-routine-create.body: Choose New schedule to run an agent on the clock, or New event trigger to run it when something happens. We'll move on the moment it exists.
flow-routine-create.title: Create a routine

flow-routine-run-now.body: Run now runs the routine immediately - same agent, same prompt, same run log - without waiting for its schedule. It is how you find out whether the prompt says what you meant before the clock does.
flow-routine-run-now.title: Fire it once, now

flow-skill-create.body: Choose New skill - the form opens and we'll walk it together, field by field.
flow-skill-create.title: Add your skill

flow-skill-field-create.body: Choose Create. We'll move on the moment it's saved.
flow-skill-field-create.title: Create it

flow-skill-field-description.body: This is the only part the model reads when deciding whether to open the skill at all - write when to reach for it, not what's inside. Then choose Next.
flow-skill-field-description.title: Say when it applies

flow-skill-field-name.body: Short and specific, like refund-policy - it's how the model refers to this skill, and it can't be changed later. Then choose Next.
flow-skill-field-name.title: Name it

flow-skill-field-source.body: Switch to Source and write the know-how itself in Markdown - the steps, the rules, the exceptions. You can refine it anytime after. Then choose Next.
flow-skill-field-source.title: Write the skill

flow-skill-improvement-accept.body: Apply it when nobody got worse. When somebody did: keep them on their version, make a fork for the agents it helped, improve it further or discard it.
flow-skill-improvement-accept.title: What you may do with it

flow-skill-improvement-agents.body: Each agent of the line comes out better, unchanged, within noise, worse or unknown, worst first, with what it fixed and broke and a link to its run.
flow-skill-improvement-agents.title: A result for every agent

flow-skill-improvement-start.body: Every agent of the line is named before anything is spent, the ones that cannot be checked with the reason, and the price comes with a limit you set.
flow-skill-improvement-start.title: Who it is checked on

flow-skill-improvement-steps.body: Understand, Changes, Check, Result and Accept, as in agent Improve. The session stops for you after Understand, after Changes and at the result.
flow-skill-improvement-steps.title: The same five steps

flow-skill-merge-changes.body: Each part says which side it comes from. A conflict shows both sides and the merged text; rewrite it if it is wrong.
flow-skill-merge-changes.title: Settle the merge

flow-skill-merge-start.body: Shows how many parts both sides changed and what proposing their texts costs. The check is priced later, at Changes.
flow-skill-merge-start.title: Merge a fork with main

flow-table-create.body: Choose New table — the form opens and we'll walk it together, field by field.
flow-table-create.title: Create the table

flow-table-field-columns.body: Choose Add column for each field a record holds, and pick its type — text, a number, a date, a select. You can change them later. Then choose Next.
flow-table-field-columns.title: Add its columns

flow-table-field-create.body: Choose Create table. We'll move on the moment it exists.
flow-table-field-create.title: Create it

flow-table-field-name.body: Name it after what one record is — Orders, Leads, Support tickets — so anyone reading or writing it knows what belongs in it. Then choose Next.
flow-table-field-name.title: Name it

flow-table-field-visibility.body: Open More options to change visibility. Private keeps the table to you; Team and Organization open it to more people. You can share it with individual people later. Then choose Next.
flow-table-field-visibility.title: Who can see it

flow-test-draft.absent: The draft is the same as the live version, so there is nothing to test yet. Change something in Build, then test it - or finish here.
flow-test-draft.body: This draft differs from the live version. Test it on a dataset before publishing.
flow-test-draft.title: Test the draft

flow-test-run.body: The cost is worked out as you choose and says what the budgets keep afterwards. Nothing runs before you press this.
flow-test-run.title: Run it for the price shown

flow-test-target.body: The draft against the live version is already chosen: both answer the same cases now, so whatever changed is the draft's doing.
flow-test-target.title: What you are testing

flow-test-verdict.body: Once both sides finish, this says whether the draft did better or worse, by how many confirmed cases. From here open the cases that broke, see what changed, or publish.
flow-test-verdict.title: Read the verdict

flow-workflow-create.body: Click here to begin. The dialog opens with a blank canvas and the ready-made templates — pick one and you land in the editor.
flow-workflow-create.title: Start a workflow

group-add-to.body: Share agents, knowledge, skills, context, apps and MCP servers with the whole department at once. Each member is told it is there.
group-add-to.title: Give it what it needs

group-members.body: The people in this department. Its lead - marked with a crown - adds and removes them; an administrator names the lead.
group-members.title: Who is in it

groups-list.body: Each group's page lists its people and everything shared with it. Choose a group when you create an agent, skill or knowledge base to keep it for that department.
groups-list.title: Your groups

groups-new.body: A group is a department or a team. Add one by hand, or add several departments at once from the templates.
groups-new.title: Add a group

improvement-accept.body: Publish the new version, or keep the changes as a draft to publish later. Nothing is accepted or published by itself.
improvement-accept.title: Accept

improvement-automatic-check.body: On the first session, tick this to test these questions again whenever the agent changes. A version that breaks one of them waits before it reaches where people use the agent.
improvement-automatic-check.title: Automatic check

improvement-changes.body: The changes the helper wrote. The session stops here: tick the ones to test and correct any wording before they are tested.
improvement-changes.title: Changes

improvement-check.body: Today's version and the changed one answer the same questions in one test. Each bar shows how far each has got, and the result opens once the test is done.
improvement-check.title: Check

improvement-details.body: Adjust the spending limit, inspect the test questions or check today’s answers. The helper’s model and instructions live in the dataset’s Settings.
improvement-details.title: Show details

improvement-guard.body: Each place people use the agent says what publishing does there: it switches at once, switches after its automatic check passes, or stays on its version.
improvement-guard.title: Where people use it

improvement-next-step.body: Each stop ends here: what the next step does and what it costs. Nothing is spent until you press it.
improvement-next-step.title: Next step

improvement-question-set.body: The questions this session will test on: where they come from, and how many help write the changes against how many are kept aside to check them.
improvement-question-set.title: Test questions

improvement-questions.body: The questions each change is tested on, as they were when the session started. Some help write the changes; the rest are kept aside to check the result.
improvement-questions.title: Test questions

improvement-results.body: First what the session came to and what you can do about it. Then the confirmed changes, and each attempt in one row that opens to its changed answers, before and after.
improvement-results.title: Result

improvement-review.body: Doubt a grade? Open the full check and send the answer to Review. A person's decision replaces the grader's, and the result is worked out again.
improvement-review.title: Review

improvement-skill-handoffs.body: Problems the helper found in one of the agent's skills. A skill is shared, so it is improved on its own, and checked on every agent that reads it.
improvement-skill-handoffs.title: Belongs to a skill

improvement-start.body: We read what went wrong and stop for you to look. You press Next step to write changes, and again to test them; each step is priced before you press. Nothing goes live until you accept it.
improvement-start.title: Improve

improvement-steps.body: Five steps. The session stops after Understand and after Changes for you to look and press Next step; a step opens once it has something to show.
improvement-steps.title: Steps

improvement-test-set.body: The agent's own test questions are already chosen and priced. Start improving is the one decision here; nothing is spent before it.
improvement-test-set.title: Time and cost

improvement-understand.body: What went wrong, sorted into what the agent can fix and what the knowledge base is missing. Answers the classifier found nothing wrong with are listed apart, as not a problem to fix. There is nothing to set here: the session stops so you can read it before the next step.
improvement-understand.title: Understand

inbox-filters.body: Findings from your watches and the nightly suggestions, urgent first. Filter by where they came from, or open Done to bring back one you declined.
inbox-filters.title: What came to you on its own

kb-documents.body: Every document the collection holds, with the status of each as it's parsed and indexed. Add more here, or preview and remove what's already there.
kb-documents.title: What's in it

kb-gaps.body: Questions agents searched this collection for and found nothing relevant to, grouped by topic. Open a topic to write the missing content, or finish a model's draft, and add it to this knowledge base - or dismiss a topic that needs none.
kb-gaps.title: What it could not answer

kb-gaps-check.body: A search can find something and the agent still not know. With AI assistance on, a model reads recent answers and thumbs-down comments for questions this knowledge base could not answer.
kb-gaps-check.title: Check the answers too

kb-header.body: The collection's name, scope and controls sit up top - refresh it, drop in files, change how they're read, or remove it.
kb-header.title: Inside a collection

kb-ingestion.body: The parser, chunking and embedding model behind this collection - what turns your files into something searchable. Change it, and new uploads follow the new settings.
kb-ingestion.title: How documents are read

kb-sync.body: Connect a drive, a site or a repo, and the collection refreshes itself from the source instead of waiting on a manual re-upload.
kb-sync.title: Keep it in step

knowledge-add-integration.body: Start a new one here - pick a connector like S3 or Google Drive, give it credentials, and it becomes available to clone into any collection that needs it.
knowledge-add-integration.title: Add a connection

knowledge-groups.body: Narrow the list to what one group was given. A group is who something reaches, so it is also how the list is grouped.
knowledge-groups.title: By department

knowledge-integrations.body: Connections shared across the organization: set up an S3 bucket, a drive, a site or a repo once here, and clone it into any collection instead of re-configuring it each time.
knowledge-integrations.title: Reusable connections

knowledge-local-services.body: Servers on your own network: register an Ollama to embed with no key, or an OCR server for LiteParse, and pick one per collection - so a knowledge base can stay entirely on your hardware.
knowledge-local-services.title: Local services

knowledge-new.body: Upload documents so your agents can answer from them. Each collection is searchable and stays private to your organization - create your first one here.
knowledge-new.title: Knowledge bases

knowledge-tabs.body: Two views of the same knowledge: the collections you've built, and a search that runs across all of them at once.
knowledge-tabs.title: Browse or search

mcp-add.body: Not in the catalog? Add a custom server by pasting its URL - for the whole organization, or just for yourself.
mcp-add.title: Bring your own

mcp-catalog.body: MCP servers are ready-made tool sets your agents can call. Connect one for the whole organization, or for yourself with your own account, then add it to an agent from its MCP servers tab.
mcp-catalog.title: Plug in tools

mcp-connect.body: Connecting a server asks how to sign in, then lets you choose exactly which of its tools your agents are allowed to call.
mcp-connect.title: Connect, then pick tools

mcp-filter.body: Search the catalog, or narrow it by category and by whether you've already connected it.
mcp-filter.title: Find a server

memory-views.body: Memories holds facts, preferences and decisions. Notes holds longer files and checklists. Search the whole store, then open an entry to see its source and manage its use.
memory-views.title: Two ways agents remember

my-claims.body: Beside notes, agents record facts, preferences and decisions with where each came from. Correct one in your own words, from a date, and the old version stays in the history; or take it out of use.
my-claims.title: What is on record about you

my-memory.body: Agents keep notes between conversations. This is yours: read what was written, stop a note being used without destroying it, or delete it outright. A note in an external memory service is named here but not shown.
my-memory.title: What agents remember about you

my-sign-ins.body: When you sign in during a browse and keep the sign-in, your agents' browser starts signed in there next time. Forget a site and the next browse starts signed out.
my-sign-ins.title: Sites you stay signed in to

nav-pinned.body: Apps you starred sit here in the sidebar, one tap away. Star one from its card or page, and unstar it the same way.
nav-pinned.title: Pinned apps

notification-bell.body: A run that failed, an approval waiting on you, a budget about to run out, a message from an app admin - it all lands here, with an in-app and email toggle for the kinds you can turn off in Settings.
notification-bell.title: Stay in the loop

org-assistant.body: Switch the organization's assistant on or off and set how it greets people. Its name, model and knowledge are edited in the Agent Builder, like any agent's.
org-assistant.title: The AI Architect

org-directory.body: Each mapping turns a directory group - an LDAP group or an OIDC groups claim - into a role here, and optionally a group. The sync applies them at every sign-in and keeps the memberships it made in step.
org-directory.title: Who the directory lets in

org-directory-new.body: Paste the group's DN or claim value and pick a role. You can only hand out roles below your own.
org-directory-new.title: Map a directory group

org-governance.body: Set the organization spending limit and manage approval waivers. Controls depend on your permissions.
org-governance.title: Budget and approvals

org-groups.body: A group is a named set of members. Share an agent, a skill, a collection or a vault secret with it, and everybody in it gets that access at once - their roles stay as they are.
org-groups.title: Share with a group

org-groups-new.body: Give it a name and, if you like, a line on what it is for. Then open its members to add people, or let a directory mapping place them when they sign in.
org-groups-new.title: Create a group

org-members.body: Everyone in the organization and the role each holds. Invite teammates, change a role, or remove someone - all from this list.
org-members.title: Who's in it

org-proactivity.body: Configure nightly suggestions, connection watches and proactive chat greetings. Choose the model, schedule and per-person budget here.
org-proactivity.title: Proactivity

org-proactivity-model.body: Choose a provider, model and vault key, then add the model profile. Creating a profile stores it immediately; Save applies it to nightly suggestions and MCP watches. These checks use this model independently of the AgenticOS starter shown in Activity.
org-proactivity-model.title: Choose the proactivity model

org-profile.body: The organization's name and avatar, shown wherever it appears. Owners and admins can change them here.
org-profile.title: Name and face

org-public-attribution.body: Show a small floating AgenticOS badge with a GitHub link on public apps, dashboards and reports, and below shared conversations.
org-public-attribution.title: AgenticOS on shared pages

org-public-live-data.body: Whether public links and embeds may show table data to people without an account. It's off by default, and each page's owner still has to confirm their page.
org-public-live-data.title: Live data on public pages

org-retention.body: A period per class - conversations, runs, documents, memory, uploads and the audit trail. A sweep runs daily and deletes for good, within whatever bounds the deployment set; the audit trail has a floor you can lengthen and never shorten.
org-retention.title: How long data lives here

org-roles.body: The permission matrix, role by role: what each may touch and how far it reaches. Sharing a single resource can widen access beyond the role, never narrow it.
org-roles.title: What each role may do

org-system-agents.body: Choose models and budgets for platform services and review their usage. Daily briefing settings are in Proactivity.
org-system-agents.title: Background services

org-voice.body: Choose the speech-to-text provider, key and language agents and channel bots inherit. Dictation and calls are switched on in each agent.
org-voice.title: Voice

organization-switcher.body: The name here is the organization you're working in. Open the menu to switch organizations, manage them or create another. Agents, knowledge and activity follow your selection.
organization-switcher.title: Choose your organization

orgs-new.body: Everything is scoped to an organization. Create one, or switch between the ones you belong to - each keeps its own agents, keys and knowledge apart.
orgs-new.title: Your organizations

personal-coding-accounts.body: Connect your coding account and explicitly allow its use here. Private cloud tasks return a diff and result archive without automatically changing shared project files.
personal-coding-accounts.title: Coding accounts

personal-model-connections.body: Connect your Claude subscription or a personal API key, then choose its models in an agent or chat. Only your signed-in runs can use personal connections.
personal-model-connections.title: Your AI connections

phone-contact.body: Select a verified SMS identity and separately allow calls, spoken reports or transfers. Choose the report language and quiet hours; changed or expired number links require a new consent review.
phone-contact.title: Your phone consent

phone-dial.body: Choose a configured route and a published voice agent, or prepare a spoken report. The request is queued once; unknown provider acceptance is never redialled automatically.
phone-dial.title: Call your own number

project-file-fullscreen.body: Open a file, then expand its reader to use the screen. The back arrow returns to the folder list.
project-file-fullscreen.title: More room for files

project-file-location.body: Computer shows your approved local folder. Shared project files contains uploaded copies for people with project access. The two locations do not synchronize automatically.
project-file-location.title: Your computer or shared files

project-graph.body: Graph view derives links and backlinks from Markdown and frontmatter. It refreshes while open, using only files you can read in this location.
project-graph.title: Explore linked notes

project-tabs.body: Start a chat in the project, add files and folders its agents work in, and set what every agent here is told. In the desktop app, you can also connect a local folder without uploading its files.
project-tabs.title: Chats, files and instructions

project-tracking.body: Review a published source agent and its accounts, then explicitly publish a private tracker with a task table and an ordinary project routine.
project-tracking.title: Keep project on track

projects-list.body: The projects you own and the ones shared with you or your departments. Every chat in one is its members' to read and join.
projects-list.title: Your projects

projects-new.body: Give ongoing work a home: instructions every agent in it reads, and files every chat in it shares.
projects-new.title: Start a project

remote-agents-list.body: Agents registered here by their A2A agent card can be picked as delegates, beside your own agents.
remote-agents-list.title: Agents from other vendors

remote-agents-register.body: Paste the address of an agent's card. It is read and checked now, and a key from the vault can go with every call.
remote-agents-register.title: Register one

routine-access.body: Use the shield on your routine to review its source accounts and resources, then choose any standing action exceptions separately.
routine-access.title: Review routine access

routine-advanced.body: Routine and watch forms start with standard execution and notification settings. Expand Advanced options to choose a version, environment, budget or delivery policy.
routine-advanced.title: Keep the defaults or fine-tune

routines-create.body: A schedule runs on the clock - every hour, weekday mornings, the first of the month. A trigger runs when something happens: a GitHub issue, an email arriving, or a signed POST from your own code.
routines-create.title: Two ways to start one

routines-list.body: Every schedule and trigger across the organization, with what it last did. An agent working while nobody is at the keyboard shows up here first.
routines-list.title: What runs without you

routines-watches.body: Watches read your own connected accounts on a schedule - reviews waiting on you, issues assigned to you - and put what is new in your inbox. Each row says when it last looked and how much of what it found still waits.
routines-watches.title: What watches your accounts

run-detail-input.body: The prompt as it was composed and sent, every tool with the description the model reads, the settings, and one bar per request - recorded from the wire, so it is what was sent rather than what the spec says.
run-detail-input.title: What the model was actually given

runs-score-against-case.body: From this menu, grade this run's answer against a case of a dataset: its checks, the tool calls it expected and, if configured, the judge. The case asking the same question is picked for you; the result is kept on the dataset.
runs-score-against-case.title: Score this run

sandboxes-connections.body: Agents that write and run code do it on these hosts. Watch the live sessions and set the ceilings from here.
sandboxes-connections.title: Where agents run code

settings-api-keys.body: A key lets a script, Postman or an MCP client act as you, without a browser. Pick what it may do; it can never do more than you can, and it stops the moment you revoke it.
settings-api-keys.title: Your API keys

settings-api-usage.body: The base URL, how a key authenticates, and the reference of every endpoint a key can call.
settings-api-usage.title: Use the API

settings-appearance.body: Pick the theme, how the chat box glows while you dictate, and how much the console moves. Each choice applies at once, in this browser.
settings-appearance.title: Appearance

settings-connected-apps.body: Apps you signed in to with this account, like Claude Code. Each acts as you within what you allowed - disconnect one to end its access at once.
settings-connected-apps.title: Connected applications

settings-mcp-connect.body: Point Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or VS Code at this organization: copy the server URL or the command for your client, and sign in through the browser.
settings-mcp-connect.title: Connect an MCP client

settings-tabs.body: Your profile, sign-in and security, notifications, and slash-commands all live behind these tabs - switch between them here.
settings-tabs.title: Your settings

sign-in-to-site.body: Open a browser on a site for you alone, sign in, and hand it back with Keep me signed in - your agents' browser starts signed in there from then on.
sign-in-to-site.title: Sign in to a site

skill-agents.body: Every agent that uses the skill, with the version it is served: main follows each new version, pinned stays on an older one, and a fork has changes of its own.
skill-agents.title: Who uses this skill

skill-catch-up.body: Merges what main changed since the fork started into the fork. The fork's agents check the merge before anything changes.
skill-catch-up.title: Catch the fork up

skill-change-version.body: Publishes a new version of the agent with only this change. A version never checked on the agent asks you to confirm first.
skill-change-version.title: Move an agent to another version

skill-content.body: The description, instructions and files the line shown serves now, to read without opening the editor.
skill-content.title: What it says

skill-edit.body: Saving never overwrites. It adds a version to the line on screen, and only the agents following that line get it.
skill-edit.title: Edit makes a new version

skill-editor-fullscreen.body: Use the expand button to read or edit the whole document. Closing the expanded editor keeps your current draft.
skill-editor-fullscreen.title: Expand the editor

skill-history.body: See what each version changed, who made it and where it came from. Restore brings an earlier one back as the newest.
skill-history.title: Every version, and the way back

skill-improve.body: Opens a step-by-step session for the line on screen: main, or the fork you picked. Nothing changes until you accept a result.
skill-improve.title: Improve the skill

skill-improvement-accept.body: Apply it when nobody got worse. When somebody did: keep them on their version, make a fork for the agents it helped, improve it further or discard it.
skill-improvement-accept.title: What you may do with it

skill-improvement-agents.body: Each agent of the line comes out better, unchanged, within noise, worse or unknown, worst first, with what it fixed and broke and a link to its run.
skill-improvement-agents.title: A result for every agent

skill-improvement-start.body: Every agent of the line is named before anything is spent, the ones that cannot be checked with the reason, and the price comes with a limit you set.
skill-improvement-start.title: Who it is checked on

skill-improvement-steps.body: Understand, Changes, Check, Result and Accept, as in agent Improve. The session stops for you after Understand, after Changes and at the result.
skill-improvement-steps.title: The same five steps

skill-improvement-test-set.body: Agents without test questions come out unknown. The skill's own questions, written from answers where it was loaded, let them be checked next time.
skill-improvement-test-set.title: Questions of the skill's own

skill-lines.body: Show the agents on main, the pinned ones, or one fork. Picking a fork also points History and Edit at it.
skill-lines.title: One line at a time

skill-merge-changes.body: Each part says which side it comes from. A conflict shows both sides and the merged text; rewrite it if it is wrong.
skill-merge-changes.title: Settle the merge

skill-merge-start.body: Shows how many parts both sides changed and what proposing their texts costs. The check is priced later, at Changes.
skill-merge-start.title: Merge a fork with main

skill-new-fork.body: New fork starts a line of its own from main's newest version. Agents moved onto it read its changes, and main's agents never see them.
skill-new-fork.title: A fork for the agents that differ

skill-test-questions.body: Questions every agent using the skill is asked when a change to it is checked. Start them here from recent answers, or empty, and edit them in the dataset.
skill-test-questions.title: Its test questions

skill-usage.body: How often each agent opened the skill in the last 30 days, and the files it read. Eval and test-panel runs are left out.
skill-usage.title: How much it is used

skills-gallery.body: Seventy ready-made skills, grouped by industry. Install one, or a whole shelf, then edit it like any other.
skills-gallery.title: Start from the gallery

skills-groups.body: Narrow the list to what one group was given. A group is who something reaches, so it is also how the list is grouped.
skills-groups.title: By department

skills-list.body: The skills you've written or installed. An agent picks the ones it needs from its Skills tab, and the same skill can serve several agents at once.
skills-list.title: Your skills

skills-new.body: A skill is a packaged set of instructions an agent can draw on for a task. Write one once here and share it across the agents that need it.
skills-new.title: Reusable skills

table-columns.body: Add a column, rename one, choose its type and whether it is optional, or archive one you no longer use. Each save is a new schema version, and records keep their values.
table-columns.title: Its columns

table-triggers.body: Run a published workflow for every record added to this table, however it was added. Filter which records start it and choose what its run starts with.
table-triggers.title: When a record is added

table-view-tabs.body: The same records as a table, as a kanban board grouped by a single-select column, or as a list. Save a view to keep its filters, sort and grouping.
table-view-tabs.title: Three ways to look

tables-catalog.body: Every table you can open: your own and the ones shared with you. Each holds typed records that people, agents and integrations read and write.
tables-catalog.title: Your tables

tables-new.body: A table is a set of records with named, typed columns. Create one here, then edit its records in the console, or let agents and the API read and write them.
tables-new.title: Structured records

vault-keys.body: Every credential in this organization, listed by name and kind. An agent references a key by its name; the value itself is shown to no one once it's saved.
vault-keys.title: What's stored

vault-new.body: API keys and other credentials live here, encrypted at rest. Agents use them to reach the tools they need, and nobody sees a stored secret again.
vault-new.title: The vault

welcome.body: This is where your team builds, runs and governs its AI agents. We'll step through each section and point out what's worth noticing - about a minute, and you can close it whenever you like.
welcome.title: Welcome to AgenticOS

workflow-canvas-fullscreen.body: This floating button expands the diagram. Use it again to return to the workflow header; your draft stays in place.
workflow-canvas-fullscreen.title: Work on the full screen
