workflow-input-contract.body: A Manual, API or Called by a workflow trigger can use simple fields or a JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 contract. The schema supports nested values and is checked before a run starts.
workflow-input-contract.title: Define the expected input

workflow-log-alerts.body: Rules that tell people when this log crosses a threshold: how many matching lines, in how long, and who hears. Anyone who can edit the workflow adds, changes or deletes them.
workflow-log-alerts.title: Its alerts

workflow-logs.body: The lines this workflow's steps wrote with a quick log, newest first. Narrow them by step, outcome or time, search the message, and add test runs. A line opens the run that wrote it.
workflow-logs.title: Its log

workflow-run-history.body: Every run of this workflow, newest first. Narrow it to failed runs or to test runs, and open one to see each step's data or retry it from the step that failed.
workflow-run-history.title: Its runs

workflow-run-questions.body: An agent in this workflow can ask for clarification. Answer here to continue its saved conversation and let the workflow proceed.
workflow-run-questions.title: Answer the agent

workflow-stats.body: This workflow's real runs over the last week, month or quarter: how many ended well, how long they took, what they cost against the month's budget, and which steps the cost and the failures came from.
workflow-stats.title: How it has been going

workflow-step-view.body: On a phone, choose step settings, input or output to give the active panel the available space. Switching panels keeps your draft.
workflow-step-view.title: Focus on one panel

workflows-list.body: Every workflow you can see, grouped by status. Filter to drafts you're still building, the published versions that run, or the archived ones. Open one to edit it, or duplicate it into a fresh copy.
workflows-list.title: Draft, published, archived

workflows-new.body: A workflow chains steps into an automation your agents run. Start one here — from a blank canvas or a template.
workflows-new.title: Build a workflow

workflows-runs.body: What ran, across every workflow you can see, newest first. Narrow it to failed runs, to test runs of drafts or to what one trigger started. Open a run to see each step's data, retry it from the step that failed, or bring its data into the editor.
workflows-runs.title: Every workflow's runs

workspace-background.body: Follow the topics your agents are working on, and return to their results.
workspace-background.title: Background work

workspace-file-fullscreen.body: Open a file, then expand its reader to use the screen. The back arrow returns to the folder list.
workspace-file-fullscreen.title: More room for files

workspace-graph.body: Graph view derives links and backlinks from Markdown and frontmatter. It refreshes while open, using only files you can read in this location.
workspace-graph.title: Explore linked notes

workspaces-browser.body: When an agent saves a file, it lands here - browse, preview and download whatever your conversations produced.
workspaces-browser.title: Your documents

workspaces-detail.body: One agent's files, folder by folder. Preview a file, or download whatever an agent produced for you.
workspaces-detail.title: Inside a folder

chat-team-room.title: Your team's room
chat-team-room.body: This conversation follows the project's sharing permissions. See who is here and use Share to check or manage its audience.

chat-team-composer.title: Talk first, ask an agent when needed
chat-team-composer.body: Post to your teammates without starting an agent. Choose an agent explicitly for an AI answer; its request joins the shared queue.

onboardingSetup.title: Welcome to {appName}
onboardingSetup.description: Get started at your own pace. Connect an app now, or head straight into your workspace.
onboardingSetup.appsDescription: Connect the tools you use through Composio. Choose each app and review its permissions before authorizing access.
onboardingSetup.opensNewTab: Opens in a new tab. Return here when you're ready.
onboardingSetup.skipHint: No app connection is required. You can connect later from Connections → Apps.

onboardingTeam.step1Subtitle: Tell us a bit about what you do so we can recommend the right specialist agents.
onboardingTeam.industryLabel: What industry or domain are you in?
onboardingTeam.step2Title: What should your AI team handle?
onboardingTeam.step2Subtitle: Select the workflows you want to delegate, automate, or accelerate.
onboardingTeam.detailsLabel: Tell us more about your workflow (optional)
onboardingTeam.detailsPlaceholder: e.g. We get lots of customer inquiries, write weekly updates, and need help drafting documentation without spending hours on it...
onboardingTeam.step3Subtitle: Choose the tools your team relies on daily. You can connect them now or anytime later from Connectors.
onboardingTeam.appsDescription: Authorize your tools through Composio with verified permissions. You can also connect them later.
onboardingTeam.opensNewTab: Opens in a new tab. Return here when ready.
onboardingTeam.skipHint: Connecting apps is completely optional. You can connect anytime later.
onboardingTeam.step4Subtitle: Here is your team structure. Your Team Lead coordinates incoming requests and delegates work to your specialists.
onboardingTeam.deployingSubtitle: Setting up models, delegation channels, and workspace...
onboardingTeam.deployingStep3: Wiring delegation hierarchy and orchestrator routing...
onboardingTeam.successSubtitle: Your Lead Agent and specialists have been created and wired together.
onboardingTeam.generatingProposal: Analyzing your profile and generating team recommendation...

orgAssistant.description: The assistant in the corner of every page, for everyone who may run agents. It is an agent like any other: its name, model and knowledge are edited in the Agent Builder, and its cost counts like any agent's.
orgAssistant.enabledHint: Off, it disappears from every page for everyone in the organization, and nobody can run it.
orgAssistant.greetingHint: What it says when somebody opens it. Leave empty for the default.
orgAssistant.needsModel: It has no model yet, so it cannot answer. Choose one under Model in the Agent Builder.
orgAssistant.title: AI Architect

organizations.accessLost: You no longer have access to that organization.
organizations.accessLostLink: That link is for an organization you no longer have access to.
organizations.accessLostLinkSwitched: That link is for an organization you no longer have access to. Showing {name} instead.
organizations.accessLostSwitched: You no longer have access to that organization. Switched to {name}.
organizations.description: Manage your organizations and switch between them.
organizations.title: Organizations

outcomes.label: Needs your attention
outcomes.loadFailed: Could not load items needing your attention

admin.accessDomainsHint: Leave empty to allow every domain. An invitation overrides this list.
admin.accessMode_closed: Nobody can register, by any route - including an invitation. To add somebody, switch to invite-only and invite them. The first account on a new deployment is always allowed.
admin.accessMode_invite_only: Only an address somebody has invited, by email or through a link scoped to its domain.
admin.accessSignupHint: Applied to the sign-up form and to signing in with a provider for the first time.
admin.adminAccessHint: What happens when an administrator acts as somebody's account.
admin.brandingDescriptionHint: Used as the page description and on link previews.
admin.brandingFaviconHint: The browser-tab icon. A square image reads best at 32 pixels.
admin.brandingIdentityHint: What this deployment calls itself, everywhere it says so.
admin.brandingLegalHint: Whose terms this deployment links to.
admin.brandingLinkHint: An absolute https address. Leave empty to keep the built-in pages.
admin.brandingLogoHint: PNG, JPEG, WebP or GIF, up to 2MB. Drawn wherever the name appears.
admin.brandingNameHint: Leave empty to keep the built-in name. Shown in the sidebar, on the sign-in page, in the browser tab and in every email this deployment sends.
admin.brandingTaglineHint: One line, shown beside the name in the browser tab and on a shared link.
admin.defaultOrganizationHint: Every new account joins it, the console opens it when nothing else is selected, and a request that names no organization acts in it.
admin.defaultOrganizationRoleHint: An invitation to this organization overrides it with the role the invitation names.
admin.eachRowSaysWhat: Each row says what was checked. Auto-refreshes every 30s.
admin.everyStatusHereComes: Live checks from this deployment. Results refresh every 30 seconds while auto-refresh is on.
admin.impersonationNoticeToggle: Email people when an administrator acts as them
admin.impersonationNoticeToggleHint: Sent once, when the impersonation starts, naming the administrator. Off, the audit trail is the only record.
admin.limitsAgentsHint: Archived agents do not count, so retiring one frees its place. Leave empty for no limit.
admin.limitsHint: How much of this deployment one account, and one organization, may take up.
admin.limitsOrganizationsHint: Counts the organizations an account owns, including the personal one it is given at sign-up. Being invited into somebody else's does not count. Leave empty for no limit.
admin.maintenanceMessageHint: What people see instead of the product. Leave empty for the default wording.
admin.maintenanceToggleHint: The API refuses every request except signing in and this section, so you can still turn it off.
admin.name: Name
admin.newAccountsHint: Where a person starts when their account is created. Existing accounts keep their organizations.
admin.noticeAnnouncementHint: Shown above every page to signed-in users, until they dismiss it. Leave empty to take it down.
admin.noticesHint: What everybody using this deployment is told, and whether it is open.
admin.orgDetailCouldNotBeRead: This organization could not be read
admin.orgNotFoundHint: It may have been deleted since the list was loaded.
admin.organizationsCouldNotBeRead: The organizations could not be read.
admin.personalOrganizationsHint: Give each new account an organization of its own. Turn off for a deployment where everyone works in one company organization.
admin.searchOrganizations: Search by name, slug or owner…
admin.serviceMapTilesDetail: Where maps in visuals get their background
admin.settingsUnreadable: Could not read the deployment settings
admin.settingsUnreadableBody: The request failed. Nothing has been changed.
admin.usersConversationsOrgsSystem: Users, conversations, organizations, and system health.

adminApns.failed: The key could not be saved.
adminApns.fileHint: Downloaded once when the key was made. It is sealed in the vault and never shown again.
adminApns.hint: Push to the iOS app goes through Apple with your company's own key: the Apple developer account the app is signed with.
adminApns.keyIdHint: Ten characters, shown beside the key in Certificates, Identifiers & Profiles, Keys.
adminApns.removed: Removed. iPhones get no notifications until a key is added.
adminApns.saved: Saved. iPhones can turn notifications on now.
adminApns.teamIdHint: Ten characters, in the developer account's Membership details.
adminApns.title: iPhone notifications
adminApns.topicHint: The identifier your build of the app is signed with.

adminDiagnostics.disable: To disable, set this in the backend and frontend .env files and restart the services:
adminDiagnostics.rejected: Collector refused the report. Check its configuration and protocol version.
adminDiagnostics.scope: Hourly installation health and version, 30-day activity buckets, grouped run/job/ingestion errors, and pseudonymous foreground users by web/desktop/mobile. No conversations, prompts, files, keys, account names or email addresses. Approximate country/region only; raw events 7 days, daily activity and aggregates 90 days.
adminDiagnostics.title: Diagnostics
adminDiagnostics.transport: Collector could not be reached. The next hourly heartbeat will try again.

adminDictation.acknowledge: I understand that a dictation's cost is no longer bounded by its maximum length, in any organization.
adminDictation.benefit: The benefit: recordings upload at about an eighth of the size. Turning this off again needs no confirmation.
adminDictation.dialogIntro: Raw PCM is the only format whose length cannot be faked. Read what changes before you turn this on.
adminDictation.hint: What a dictation may be uploaded as, in every organization's composer, hosted pages and widgets.
adminDictation.riskLength: A compressed recording's length is read from the file's own header. A crafted file can understate it, so one dictation can carry far more audio than the maximum length - up to about 40 times as much within the size cap.
adminDictation.riskPublic: On public widgets and hosted pages, anyone holding the link can send such files. Transcription is billed to the organization's provider account and is outside agent budgets, so the per-link rate limit no longer bounds the cost to the documented worst case.
adminDictation.riskScope: It applies to every organization on this deployment.
adminDictation.title: Dictation audio
adminDictation.toggleHint: Off, browsers record 16 kHz mono PCM WAV. Its length is its size, so the longest dictation bounds what one recording costs. On, uploads are about half the size, at the risks turning it on lists.

agents.agentAposSBehaviour: The agent's behaviour lives here, not in code. Be specific about what it should do, what it should refuse, and how it should cite. Markdown, and the model reads the structure - headings and lists are what make a long prompt followable, so being able to see them rendered is the point of the preview.
agents.agentAposSOwn: This agent's own monthly spending limit. The organization's limit still applies on top - an agent can tighten it, never loosen it. The step limit catches the other kind of runaway: a tool loop that is cheap per call and never finishes.
agents.agentCannotBePublished: This agent cannot be published yet
agents.agentConfigurationNotCode: An agent is an assistant with its own instructions, knowledge and tools. Build one here, publish it, and people use it in chat, in Slack or Telegram, or through the API.
agents.categoriesHint: Broad groups - support, finance, internal. The catalog filters by these.
agents.chatOnlyNotSlack: Chat only - not on Slack or Telegram
agents.connectServerOrganizationBecomes: Connect a server for the organization and it becomes bindable here. A personal connection is for your own chat and is refused at publish, so an agent everyone runs never depends on whose credential is behind it.
agents.createOneGiveInstructions: Create one, give it instructions and a few capabilities, then publish it.
agents.discoveryHelp: Labels for finding this agent. They are saved at once and are not part of the published spec, so retagging never needs a publish. The server lower-cases, trims and de-duplicates them.
agents.draftAsStandsWhat: The draft as it stands: what reaches this agent, and what it reaches for. A dashed box is something nothing is attached to.
agents.draftAsTested: Draft as the run tested it
agents.eachPublishFreezesSpec: Each publish freezes a spec. Runs record the version, so what an agent did last Tuesday stays answerable after a dozen edits. Restoring publishes a new version copied from the old one - the timeline shows that a rollback happened rather than pretending the bad version never existed.
agents.firstPublishNext: It is live in chat and over the API. Next, choose where else people reach it - a website widget, a hosted page, Slack or Telegram.
agents.fixSavesTheDraft: A fix saves the draft and checks it again. Publishing stays a step of its own.
agents.fixStopSharingUnbound: Stop sharing what this agent cannot share
agents.howAgentAsksIts: How this agent asks its model to behave, on top of whatever the model profile already sets. A setting nobody touches is not sent at all - that is deliberate rather than tidy: reasoning models reject a temperature outright, so an agent that never chose one must not have one sent on its behalf. A provider that does not implement a setting ignores it. Reasoning itself is a capability, below.
agents.howManyModelRequests: How many model requests one run may make. A tool loop hits this long before it costs enough to hit a budget.
agents.identityHelp: Saved with the draft. Renaming keeps the handle @{slug}, so delegations and mentions wired to it keep working.
agents.improveFromGaps: Improve this agent from these gaps
agents.loopGuardHint: A run that keeps making the same calls is told to change approach, and stopped if it goes on - with the reason, before the steps or the budget run out.
agents.mcpServersDescription: External tools this agent may call, from <servers>the catalog</servers>. Bind a server to the organization's account, which answers for everybody, or to each person's own account, which they connect themselves. A member's connection is never bound directly - an agent everyone runs cannot depend on whose credential is behind it.
agents.mcpToolLoad: These MCP servers give the model {count} tools on every request - roughly {tokens, number} tokens before anyone types, and more tools than a model chooses between well. Tool search keeps them out of the way until the agent looks one up.
agents.monthlyUsdHint: Runs stop once this agent spends this much in a calendar month. Blank leaves only the organization's limit.
agents.namedPointersAtPublished: A publish mints a version; putting it somewhere is a separate decision. An environment either waits to be promoted onto or follows every publish. Production follows while it is the only environment; pin it once a dev or staging sits beside it. A bot bound to an environment serves its version.
agents.noAgentHereMatches: No agent here matches that filter and search.
agents.noModelNeedsConnections: Your organization has no model yet, and an agent needs one to publish. Adding a model needs the "Manage connections" permission - ask an admin to add one.
agents.nobodyHasSharedAgent: Nobody has shared an agent with you yet.
agents.ownedByWorkflow: This agent is configured in a workflow step and versioned with that workflow. Change it there.
agents.publishAgentChatWith: Publish this agent to chat with it - the chat runs the published version
agents.removesAgentEveryVersion: This removes the agent, every version of it and every share pointing at it. Its past runs are kept for the record. Archive instead if you only want it to stop.
agents.removesAgentEveryVersion2: This removes the agent, every version of it and every share pointing at it. Its past runs are kept for the record. Archive instead if you only want it to stop.
agents.spendsWithoutCeilingIts: Spends without a ceiling of its own
agents.squareImagesLookBest: Square images look best. Up to 2MB.
agents.stopsAnsweringEverywhereAvailable: It stops answering everywhere it is available. Its versions, runs and history are kept, and it can be restored.
agents.stopsAnsweringEverywhereAvailable2: It stops answering everywhere it is available. Its versions, runs and history are kept, and it can be restored.
agents.systemAgentReadOnly: Only an organization administrator can change a system agent. You can read how it works here.
agents.tagsHint: Anything narrower you want to search by later.
agents.twoLimitsWorthKnowing: Per server, this agent can be narrowed to some of its tools - within what the connection allows - and set to stop for a person's approval before its writes or before every call. Nothing waits for approval unless you set it here.
agents.whatAgentCanDo: What this agent can do, and where it keeps what it produces. Nothing waits for a person until you set Always ask on it.
agents.youAreSupportCopilot: You are Support Copilot. Answer from the product wiki and cite the document you used. If the wiki does not cover it, say so rather than guessing.

compare.description: Make a table and explain a choice from provided facts.
compare.prompt:
Compare these fictional offers in a table and recommend one. Priorities: no more than €100/month, at least 5 seats, support under 24 hours.

A: €80/month, 5 seats, 48-hour support.
B: €95/month, 8 seats, 12-hour support.
C: €120/month, 15 seats, 4-hour support.
Do not browse or assume missing facts.
compare.result:
B meets all three requirements: €95/month, 8 seats, 12-hour support.
A meets price and seat requirements but not support.
C exceeds the budget.
compare.title: Compare three offers

document.description: Find an answer grounded in a short fictional policy.
document.prompt:
Answer using only this fictional policy and quote the supporting sentence.

Northwind demo policy: Travel over €500 needs manager approval before booking. Expense reports must be submitted within 14 days. The policy does not mention home-office equipment.

Do I need approval before booking a €650 trip? What does it say about a home-office monitor?
document.result:
The €650 trip needs approval before booking: “Travel over €500 needs manager approval before booking.”
This policy contains no rule about a home-office monitor.
document.title: Ask a question about a document

meeting.description: Get a useful plan without files or integrations.
meeting.prompt:
Turn these fictional meeting notes into an action plan with an owner and due date for each item. Flag missing information rather than inventing it.

Northwind demo team: Maya will prepare the proposal by Friday. Leo will check the budget. The client needs a status update on Wednesday. We have not assigned the update or a budget deadline.
meeting.result:
Maya — prepare proposal — Friday.
Leo — check budget — deadline not specified.
Client update — Wednesday — owner not assigned.
Confirm the budget deadline and who will send the update.
meeting.title: Turn meeting notes into an action plan
